verses.1:1: So Solomon, the son of David, was strengthened in his kingdom, and the Lord his God was with him and magnified him to the heights.
verses.1:2: And Solomon gave orders to all Israel: to the tribunes and centurions, the leaders and judges of all Israel, and the heads of the families.
verses.1:3: And he went with the whole multitude to the high place of Gibeon, where the tent of the covenant of God was, which Moses the servant of God made in the wilderness.
verses.1:4: However, David had brought the ark of God from Kiriath-jearim to the place that he had prepared for it and where he had pitched a tent for it, that is, in Jerusalem.
verses.1:5: The bronze altar also, which Bezalel the son of Uri, the son of Hur, had fashioned, was there before the tent of the Lord; and Solomon and the whole assembly sought it out.
verses.1:6: And Solomon went up to the bronze altar before the tent of the covenant of the Lord, and offered one thousand sacrifices on it.
verses.1:7: Now look, on that very night God appeared to him, saying, "Ask what you wish, so that I may give it to you."
verses.1:8: And Solomon said to God, "You have shown great mercy to David my father, and have appointed me king in his place.
verses.1:9: Now therefore, Lord God, let Your word be fulfilled that You promised to David my father, for You have made me king over Your numerous people, who are as innumerable as the dust of the earth.
verses.1:10: Give me wisdom and understanding, so that I may go in and go out before Your people; for who can worthily judge this people of Yours, who are so great?"
verses.1:11: Then God said to Solomon, "Because this pleased your heart more, and you did not ask for riches, possessions, and glory, nor the lives of those who hated you, nor even very many days of life, but have requested wisdom and knowledge so that you may be able to judge My people over whom I have appointed you king,
verses.1:12: wisdom and knowledge have been given to you; moreover, I will give you riches, possessions, and glory, such that no one among the kings, before you or after you, will have been like you."
verses.1:13: So Solomon came from the high place of Gibeon to Jerusalem, before the tent of the covenant, and reigned over Israel.
verses.1:14: And he gathered for himself chariots and horsemen, and he came to have one thousand four hundred chariots and twelve thousand horsemen; and he placed them in the chariot cities and with the king in Jerusalem.
verses.1:15: And the king supplied silver and gold in Jerusalem like stones, and cedars like the sycamores that grow in the plains in great abundance.
verses.1:16: Now horses were brought to him from Egypt and from Kue by the king's merchants, who went and bought them for a price:
verses.1:17: a four-horse chariot for six hundred pieces of silver, and a horse for one hundred fifty; similarly, purchasing was carried on from all the kingdoms of the Hittites and from the kings of Syria.
verses.1:18: Now Solomon resolved to build a house for the name of the Lord, and a palace for himself.
verses.2:1: And he counted seventy thousand men carrying loads on their shoulders, and eighty thousand to cut stones in the mountains, and three thousand six hundred as their overseers.
verses.2:2: He also sent to Hiram, king of Tyre, saying, "Just as you dealt with David my father, and sent him cedar timber so that he might build a house for himself in which he also lived,
verses.2:3: so deal with me, that I may build a house for the name of the Lord my God, to consecrate it for burning incense before Him, and for sending up fragrant spices in smoke, and for the perpetual presentation of the loaves, and for burnt offerings morning and evening, on the Sabbaths also, and on the new moons, and on the solemn feasts of the Lord our God forever, which have been commanded to Israel.
verses.2:4: For the house that I desire to build is great; for our God is great above all gods.
verses.2:5: Who then will be able to prevail so as to build a worthy house for Him? If heaven and the heavens of heavens cannot contain Him, how great am I that I should be able to build a house for Him? But for this only, that incense may be burned before Him.
verses.2:6: Send me therefore a skilled man who knows how to work in gold and silver, bronze and iron, purple, crimson, and blue, and who knows how to carve engravings with these craftsmen whom I have with me in Judea and Jerusalem, whom David my father prepared.
verses.2:7: Send me also cedar, juniper, and pine timber from Lebanon; for I know that your servants know how to cut timber from Lebanon, and my servants will be with your servants,
verses.2:8: so that very much timber may be prepared for me. For the house that I desire to build is exceedingly great and renowned.
verses.2:9: Furthermore, to the workmen who are to cut the timber, your servants, I will give as provisions twenty thousand kors of wheat, and as many kors of barley, and twenty thousand metretes of wine, and also twenty thousand seahs of oil."
verses.2:10: Then Hiram, king of Tyre, said in a letter that he had sent to Solomon, "Because the Lord loved His people, for that reason He made you reign over them."
verses.2:11: And he added, saying, "Blessed be the Lord God of Israel, who made heaven and earth, who has given King David a wise, learned, discerning, and prudent son to build a house for the Lord and a palace for himself.
verses.2:12: Therefore I have sent you a prudent and most knowledgeable man, Hiram my father,
verses.2:13: the son of a woman from the daughters of Dan, whose father was a Tyrian, who knows how to work in gold and silver, bronze and iron, marble and wood, in purple also, and blue, and fine linen, and crimson; and who knows how to engrave every carving and to devise prudently whatever is necessary in the work, with your craftsmen and with the craftsmen of my lord David, your father.
verses.2:14: Therefore send to your servants the wheat and barley, and the oil and wine that you promised, my lord.
verses.2:15: As for us, we will cut timber from Lebanon, as much as you need, and we will bring it in rafts by sea to Joppa; and it will be yours to transport it to Jerusalem."
verses.2:16: So Solomon counted all the proselyte men who were in the land of Israel, after the numbering that David his father had conducted, and there were found one hundred fifty thousand, and three thousand six hundred.
verses.2:17: And from them he assigned seventy thousand to carry burdens on their shoulders, and eighty thousand to cut stones in the mountains, and three thousand six hundred as overseers of the works of the people.
verses.3:1: And Solomon began to build the house of the Lord in Jerusalem on Mount Moriah, which had been shown to David his father, in the place that David had prepared on the threshing floor of Ornan the Jebusite.
verses.3:2: Now he began to build in the second month, in the fourth year of his reign.
verses.3:3: And these are the foundations that Solomon laid to build the house of God: in length, sixty cubits by the first measure; in width, twenty cubits.
verses.3:4: And the portico before the front, which extended in length according to the measure of the width of the house, was twenty cubits; furthermore, the height was one hundred twenty cubits; and he gilded it on the inside with the purest gold.
verses.3:5: He also covered the greater house with planks of fir wood, and fastened plates of refined gold throughout; and he carved on it palm trees and what resembled small chains intertwining with one another.
verses.3:6: He also paved the floor of the temple with the most precious marble, with great beauty.
verses.3:7: Moreover, the gold was most thoroughly tested, with plates of which he covered the house, and its beams, and doorposts, and walls, and doors; and he engraved cherubim on the walls.
verses.3:8: He also made the house of the Holy of Holies: its length, according to the width of the house, was twenty cubits, and its width likewise was twenty cubits; and he covered it with gold plates of about six hundred talents.
verses.3:9: Moreover, he made gold nails such that each nail weighed fifty shekels; he also covered the upper rooms with gold.
verses.3:10: He also made two cherubim in the house of the Holy of Holies, of statuary work, and covered them with gold.
verses.3:11: The wings of the cherubim extended twenty cubits, so that one wing measured five cubits and touched the wall of the house, and the other, measuring five cubits, touched the wing of the other cherub.
verses.3:12: Similarly, a wing of the other cherub measured five cubits and touched the wall, and its other wing, of five cubits, met the wing of the other cherub.
verses.3:13: Therefore the wings of both cherubim were spread out and extended across twenty cubits; and they themselves stood upright on their feet, and their faces were turned toward the outer house.
verses.3:14: He also made the veil of blue, purple, crimson, and fine linen, and wove cherubim into it.
verses.3:15: Before the doors of the temple he also made two columns that measured thirty-five cubits in height; moreover, their capitals were five cubits.
verses.3:16: He also made what resembled small chains in the oracle, and set them on top of the capitals of the columns; and also one hundred pomegranates, which he placed between the small chains.
verses.3:17: He also set the columns themselves in the vestibule of the temple, one on the right and the other on the left; the one that was on the right he called Jachin, and the one on the left, Boaz.
verses.4:1: He also made a bronze altar, twenty cubits in length, and twenty cubits in width, and ten cubits in height.
verses.4:2: He also made a cast sea, ten cubits from rim to rim, round all around; it had a height of five cubits, and a cord of thirty cubits went around its circumference.
verses.4:3: There was also a likeness of oxen beneath it, and for ten cubits certain carvings on the outside encircled the belly of the sea, as it were in two rows. Now the oxen were cast,
verses.4:4: and the sea itself was set upon twelve oxen, of which three faced toward the north, and another three toward the west; moreover, three others faced the south, and the three that remained, the east, having the sea placed upon them; and the hindquarters of the oxen were inward under the sea.
verses.4:5: Furthermore, its thickness had the measure of a handbreadth, and its rim was like the rim of a cup, or of a lily curving outward; and it held three thousand metretes.
verses.4:6: He also made ten basins, and he placed five on the right and five on the left, so that they might wash in them all the things that they were about to offer for a burnt offering; whereas the priests washed themselves in the sea.
verses.4:7: Now he also made ten golden lampstands according to the form in which they had been commanded to be made, and he placed them in the temple, five on the right and five on the left.
verses.4:8: He also made ten tables, and he placed them in the temple, five on the right and five on the left; and also one hundred golden bowls.
verses.4:9: He also made the court of the priests, and the great hall, and doors in the hall, which he covered with bronze.
verses.4:10: Moreover, he placed the sea on the right side, facing the east, toward the south.
verses.4:11: Now Hiram made the pots, and the meat forks, and the bowls; and he completed all the work of the king in the house of God:
verses.4:12: that is, the two pillars, and the capitals, and the heads, and, as it were, certain networks that would cover the heads upon the capitals;
verses.4:13: also four hundred pomegranates, and two networks, so that two rows of pomegranates were joined to each network, which would cover over the capitals and the heads of the pillars.
verses.4:14: He also made the bases, and the basins, which he placed upon the bases:
verses.4:15: one sea, and also twelve oxen under the sea,
verses.4:16: and the pots, and the meat forks, and the bowls. Hiram his father made all the vessels for Solomon in the house of the Lord out of the purest bronze.
verses.4:17: In the region of the Jordan, the king cast them in clay ground between Succoth and Zeredathah.
verses.4:18: Now the multitude of the vessels was innumerable, so that the weight of the bronze was unknown.
verses.4:19: And Solomon made all the vessels of the house of God, and the golden altar, and the tables, and upon them the loaves of presentation;
verses.4:20: also the lampstands with their lamps, of the purest gold, so that they might shine before the inner sanctuary according to the rite;
verses.4:21: and certain floral ornaments, and the lamps, and the golden tongs; all were made of the purest gold.
verses.4:22: Also the incense burners, and the censers, and the bowls, and the small mortars were of the purest gold. And he carved the doors of the inner temple, that is, into the Holy of Holies, and the doors of the temple on the outside were golden. And thus all the work that Solomon did in the house of the Lord was completed.
verses.5:1: Therefore Solomon brought in all the things that David his father had vowed; he placed the silver, and the gold, and all the vessels in the treasuries of the house of God.
verses.5:2: After these things he assembled the elders of Israel, and all the leaders of the tribes, and the heads of the families from the sons of Israel to Jerusalem, so that they might bring the ark of the covenant of the Lord from the city of David, which is Zion.
verses.5:3: So all the men of Israel came to the king on the festival day of the seventh month.
verses.5:4: And when all the elders of Israel had come, the Levites carried the ark,
verses.5:5: and they brought it in, and all the furnishings of the tabernacle. Moreover, the priests with the Levites carried the vessels of the sanctuary that were in the tabernacle.
verses.5:6: Now King Solomon, and the entire assembly of Israel, and all who were assembled before the ark, were sacrificing rams and oxen without any number, for so great was the multitude of the sacrifices.
verses.5:7: And the priests brought the ark of the covenant of the Lord into its place, that is, to the inner sanctuary of the temple, into the Holy of Holies, beneath the wings of the cherubim,
verses.5:8: so that the cherubim spread out their wings over the place in which the ark had been placed, and covered the ark itself along with its poles.
verses.5:9: Now the ends of the poles by which the ark was carried, because they were a little longer, were visible before the inner sanctuary; but if anyone was a little outside, he could not see them. So the ark has been there until the present day.
verses.5:10: And there was nothing else in the ark except the two tablets that Moses had placed at Horeb, when the Lord gave the law to the sons of Israel as they came out of Egypt.
verses.5:11: Now when the priests had come out of the sanctuary (for all the priests who could be found there were sanctified, and at that time the courses and the order of the ministries had not yet been divided among them),
verses.5:12: both the Levites and the singers, that is, those who were under Asaph, and those who were under Heman, and those who were under Jeduthun, their sons and their brothers, clothed in fine linen, were resounding with cymbals, and harps, and lyres, standing at the eastern side of the altar; and with them were one hundred and twenty priests sounding trumpets.
verses.5:13: Therefore, when all of them together were sounding in unison with trumpets, and voice, and cymbals, and instruments, and various kinds of music, and lifting their voice on high, the sound was heard far away, so that when they had begun to praise the Lord and to say, "Give thanks to the Lord, because He is good, because His mercy is forever," the house of God was filled with a cloud,
verses.5:14: and the priests could not stand and minister because of the thick darkness. For the glory of the Lord had filled the house of God.
verses.6:1: Then Solomon said, "The Lord has promised that He would dwell in thick darkness;
verses.6:2: but I have built a house for His name, so that He might dwell there forever."
verses.6:3: And the king turned his face and blessed the entire multitude of Israel (for the whole crowd was standing attentively), and said,
verses.6:4: "Blessed be the Lord God of Israel, who has fulfilled in deed what He spoke to my father David, saying,
verses.6:5: 'From the day on which I brought My people out of the land of Egypt, I did not choose a city from all the tribes of Israel so that a house might be built in it for My name, nor did I choose any other man to be leader among the people of Israel;
verses.6:6: but I chose Jerusalem so that My name may be in it, and I chose David so that I might appoint him over My people Israel.'
verses.6:7: Now when it had been the desire of my father David to build a house for the name of the Lord God of Israel,
verses.6:8: the Lord said to him, 'Because this was your desire, to build a house for My name, you indeed did well to have such a desire;
verses.6:9: yet you will not build the house; rather, your son who will come forth from your loins, he himself will build the house for My name.'
verses.6:10: Therefore the Lord has fulfilled His word that He had spoken, and I have risen in place of my father David and sat upon the throne of Israel, just as the Lord spoke, and I have built the house for the name of the Lord God of Israel.
verses.6:11: And in it I have placed the ark in which is the covenant of the Lord that He made with the sons of Israel."
verses.6:12: Then he stood before the altar of the Lord, opposite the entire multitude of Israel, and stretched out his hands.
verses.6:13: For indeed Solomon had made a bronze platform and had placed it in the middle of the basilica, measuring five cubits in length, five cubits in width, and three cubits in height; and he stood upon it, and then, with bent knees facing the entire multitude of Israel and with palms raised toward heaven,
verses.6:14: he said, "Lord God of Israel, there is no god like You in heaven and on earth, You who keep covenant and mercy with Your servants who walk before You with all their heart,
verses.6:15: who have performed for Your servant my father David all that You had spoken to him; and what You had promised with Your mouth, You have fulfilled in deed, just as the present time also proves.
verses.6:16: Now therefore, Lord God of Israel, fulfill for Your servant my father David all that You spoke, saying, 'A man from you will not be lacking before Me to sit upon the throne of Israel, provided only that your sons guard their ways and walk in My law, just as you also have walked before Me.'
verses.6:17: And now, Lord God of Israel, let Your word that You spoke to Your servant David be confirmed.
verses.6:18: Is it then believable that God should dwell with mankind on the earth? If heaven and the heavens of heavens do not contain You, how much more this house that I have built?
verses.6:19: Yet it has been made for this alone: that You may regard the prayer of Your servant and his supplication, Lord my God, and hear the petitions that Your servant pours out before You,
verses.6:20: that You may open Your eyes upon this house day and night, upon the place in which You promised that Your name would be invoked,
verses.6:21: and that You would hear the prayer that Your servant prays in it; and may You hear the petitions of Your servant and of Your people Israel. Whoever prays in this place, hear from Your dwelling, that is, from the heavens, and show mercy.
verses.6:22: If anyone sins against his neighbor, and comes prepared to swear against him, and binds himself with a curse before the altar in this house,
verses.6:23: You will hear from heaven and execute judgment on Your servants, so that You repay the wicked man his way upon his own head, and vindicate the righteous man, rewarding him according to his righteousness.
verses.6:24: If Your people Israel are defeated by enemies (for they will sin against You), and turning back they repent, and implore Your name, and plead in this place,
verses.6:25: You will hear from heaven; and pardon the sin of Your people Israel, and bring them back to the land that You gave to them and to their fathers.
verses.6:26: If, when heaven is shut, rain does not fall because of the sins of the people, and they plead with You in this place, and confess Your name, and turn back from their sins when You afflict them,
verses.6:27: hear from heaven, Lord, and forgive the sins of Your servants and of Your people Israel, and teach them the good way along which they should walk, and give rain to the land that You have given to Your people to possess.
verses.6:28: If famine arises in the land, and pestilence, blight and mildew, and locust and caterpillar, and enemies, having laid waste the regions, besiege the gates of the city, and every plague and sickness presses hard,
verses.6:29: if anyone of Your people Israel pleads, recognizing his own plague and sickness, and spreads out his hands in this house,
verses.6:30: You will hear from heaven, namely, from Your lofty dwelling; and show mercy, and repay each one according to his ways, which You know he has in his heart (for You alone know the hearts of the sons of men),
verses.6:31: so that they may fear You and walk in Your ways all the days that they live upon the face of the land that You gave to our fathers.
verses.6:32: And as for the foreigner also, who is not of Your people Israel, if he comes from a distant land because of Your great name, and because of Your strong hand and Your outstretched arm, and worships in this place,
verses.6:33: You will hear from heaven, Your most steadfast dwelling, and do everything for which that stranger calls upon You, so that all the peoples of the earth may know Your name, and fear You as Your people Israel does, and recognize that Your name has been invoked upon this house that I have built.
verses.6:34: If Your people go out to war against their adversaries by the way on which You send them, they will worship You facing the direction in which this city is, which You have chosen, and the house that I have built for Your name;
verses.6:35: You will hear from heaven their petitions and supplication, and may You execute vengeance.
verses.6:36: Now if they sin against You (for there is no man who does not sin), and You become angry with them and hand them over to enemies, and they lead them away captive to a distant land, or indeed one that is nearby,
verses.6:37: and turning back in their heart in the land to which they had been led captive, they repent and plead with You in the land of their captivity, saying, 'We have sinned; we have acted wickedly, we have dealt unjustly,'
verses.6:38: and return to You with all their heart and with all their soul in the land of their captivity to which they were led, they will worship You facing the direction of their land that You gave to their fathers, and of the city that You have chosen, and of the house that I have built for Your name;
verses.6:39: You will hear from heaven, that is, from Your steadfast dwelling, their petitions, and may You execute judgment and forgive Your people, although sinful;
verses.6:40: for You are my God; please, let Your eyes be open, and let Your ears be attentive to the prayer that is made in this place.
verses.6:41: Now therefore arise, Lord God, into Your resting place, You and the ark of Your strength; let Your priests, Lord God, be clothed with salvation, and let Your holy ones rejoice in good things.
verses.6:42: Lord God, do not turn away the face of Your anointed one; remember the mercies of Your servant David."
verses.7:1: And when Solomon had finished pouring out petitions, fire came down from heaven and devoured the burnt offerings and the sacrifices, and the majesty of the Lord filled the house.
verses.7:2: And the priests were not able to enter the temple of the Lord, because the majesty of the Lord had filled the temple of the Lord.
verses.7:3: Moreover, all the sons of Israel were watching the fire coming down and the glory of the Lord upon the house; and falling face down to the ground upon the pavement laid with stone, they worshiped and praised the Lord, because He is good, because His mercy is forever.
verses.7:4: Now the king and all the people were offering sacrifices before the Lord.
verses.7:5: So King Solomon slaughtered offerings: twenty-two thousand oxen and one hundred twenty thousand rams; and the king and the entire people dedicated the house of God.
verses.7:6: And the priests were standing in their duties, and the Levites at the instruments of the songs of the Lord, which King David made to praise the Lord, "For His mercy is eternal," singing the hymns of David by their hands; moreover, the priests were sounding trumpets before them, and all Israel was standing.
verses.7:7: Solomon also consecrated the middle of the courtyard before the temple of the Lord, for he had offered there the burnt offerings and the fat of the peace offerings, because the bronze altar that he had made could not hold the burnt offerings and the sacrifices and the fat.
verses.7:8: So Solomon observed the festival at that time for seven days, and all Israel with him, a very great assembly, from the entrance of Hamath to the brook of Egypt.
verses.7:9: And on the eighth day he held a convocation, because he had dedicated the altar for seven days and had celebrated the festival for seven days.
verses.7:10: Therefore, on the twenty-third day of the seventh month, he sent the peoples away to their tents, joyful and glad over the good that the Lord had done for David, and for Solomon, and for His people Israel.
verses.7:11: And Solomon completed the house of the Lord and the house of the king, and everything that he had planned in his heart to do in the house of the Lord and in his own house, and he prospered.
verses.7:12: Now the Lord appeared to him by night and said, "I have heard your prayer, and I have chosen this place for Myself as a house of sacrifice.
verses.7:13: If I shut heaven and rain does not fall, and I command and order the locust to devour the land, and I send pestilence among My people,
verses.7:14: and My people, upon whom My name has been invoked, turning back, plead with Me and seek out My face and repent from their most wicked ways, then I will hear from heaven, and be merciful toward their sins, and heal their land.
verses.7:15: My eyes also will be open, and My ears alert to the prayer of the one who prays in this place.
verses.7:16: For I have chosen and consecrated this place, so that My name may be there forever, and My eyes and My heart may remain there for all days.
verses.7:17: As for you also, if you walk before Me just as your father David walked, and act according to everything that I have commanded you, and keep My statutes and judgments,
verses.7:18: I will raise up the throne of your kingdom, just as I promised to your father David, saying, 'A man will not be taken away from your lineage to be ruler in Israel.'
verses.7:19: But if you turn away and abandon My statutes and My precepts that I have set before you, and going off you serve foreign gods and worship them,
verses.7:20: I will uproot you from My land that I have given to you, and this house, which I have consecrated for My name, I will cast away from My presence, and I will hand it over as a parable and as an example to all peoples.
verses.7:21: And this house will become a proverb to all who pass by, and they will say in astonishment, 'Why has the Lord done so to this land and to this house?'
verses.7:22: And they will answer, 'Because they abandoned the Lord God of their fathers, who brought them out of the land of Egypt, and took hold of foreign gods, and worshiped them and revered them; therefore all these evils have come upon them.'"
verses.8:1: Now when twenty years had been completed after Solomon built the house of the Lord and his own house,
verses.8:2: he built the cities that Hiram had given to Solomon, and he made the sons of Israel dwell there.
verses.8:3: He also went to Hamath-zobah and took possession of it.
verses.8:4: And he built Palmyra in the desert, and he built other very strongly fortified cities in Hamath.
verses.8:5: And he constructed Upper Beth-horon and Lower Beth-horon, walled cities having gates and bars and bolts;
verses.8:6: also Baalath and all the very strong cities that belonged to Solomon, and all the cities for chariots and the cities for horsemen. Everything that Solomon desired and planned, he built in Jerusalem, and in Lebanon, and in the entire land of his dominion.
verses.8:7: All the people who had been left from the Hittites, and the Amorites, and the Perizzites, and the Hivites, and the Jebusites, who were not of the lineage of Israel,
verses.8:8: from their sons and from their descendants, whom the sons of Israel had not killed, Solomon subjugated as tributaries, to this day.
verses.8:9: However, of the sons of Israel he appointed none to serve in the works of the king; for they themselves were fighting men, and chief leaders, and commanders of his chariots and horsemen.
verses.8:10: Now all the commanders of the army of King Solomon were two hundred fifty, who instructed the people.
verses.8:11: Now he moved the daughter of Pharaoh from the city of David into the house that he had built for her. For the king said, "My wife will not dwell in the house of David king of Israel, because it has been sanctified, since the ark of the Lord has entered into it."
verses.8:12: Then Solomon offered burnt offerings to the Lord upon the altar of the Lord, which he had constructed before the portico,
verses.8:13: so that offerings might be made on it each day according to the command of Moses, on the Sabbaths and on the first days of the month, and on the feast days, three times a year—that is, at the solemn feast of Unleavened Bread, and at the solemn feast of Weeks, and at the solemn feast of Tabernacles.
verses.8:14: And he appointed, according to the arrangement of his father David, the duties of the priests in their ministries, and the Levites in their order, to praise and minister before the priests according to the rite of each day, and the gatekeepers in their divisions, gate by gate; for so David, the man of God, had commanded.
verses.8:15: Nor did the priests or the Levites depart from the commands of the king in all that he had commanded, and in the guarding of the treasuries.
verses.8:16: Solomon had all the expenses prepared from the day on which he laid the foundation of the house of the Lord until the day on which he completed it.
verses.8:17: Then Solomon went to Ezion-geber and to Elath on the shore of the Red Sea, which is in the land of Edom.
verses.8:18: And Hiram sent him ships by the hands of his servants, and sailors skilled in the sea; and they went with the servants of Solomon to Ophir, and took from there four hundred fifty talents of gold, and brought it to King Solomon.
verses.9:1: The queen of Sheba also, when she had heard of the fame of Solomon, came to test him with riddles in Jerusalem, with great wealth and camels that carried spices, and a very great amount of gold, and precious gems. And when she had come to Solomon, she spoke to him of all that was in her heart.
verses.9:2: And Solomon explained to her all that she had put forward; and there was nothing that he did not make clear to her.
verses.9:3: After she saw these things—namely, the wisdom of Solomon, and the house that he had built,
verses.9:4: and also the food of his table, and the dwellings of the servants, and the duties of his attendants and their garments, the cupbearers also and their robes, and the sacrifices that he offered in the house of the Lord—there was no longer any spirit in her for astonishment.
verses.9:5: And she said to the king, "The report is true that I had heard in my land concerning your virtues and your wisdom.
verses.9:6: I did not believe those reporting it until I myself had come, and my eyes had seen, and I had verified that scarcely half of your wisdom had been told to me; you have surpassed the fame by your virtues.
verses.9:7: Blessed are your men, and blessed are your servants, who stand before you at all times and hear your wisdom.
verses.9:8: Blessed be the Lord your God, who willed to appoint you upon His throne, king of the Lord your God. Because God loves Israel and wills to preserve them forever, therefore He has placed you over them as king, so that you may execute judgments and justice."
verses.9:9: And she gave the king one hundred twenty talents of gold, and exceedingly many spices, and most precious gems; there were no spices such as these that the queen of Sheba gave to King Solomon.
verses.9:10: Moreover, the servants of Hiram with the servants of Solomon brought gold from Ophir, and thyine wood, and most precious gems,
verses.9:11: from which the king made—that is, from the thyine wood—steps in the house of the Lord and in the royal house, and also lyres and harps for the singers; such wood was never seen in the land of Judah.
verses.9:12: And King Solomon gave to the queen of Sheba all that she desired and asked for, and much more than she had brought to him; and she turned back and went to her own land with her servants.
verses.9:13: Now the weight of the gold that was brought to Solomon each year was six hundred sixty-six talents of gold,
verses.9:14: apart from that sum which the envoys of various nations and the merchants were accustomed to bring, and all the kings of Arabia and the satraps of the lands, who brought in gold and silver to Solomon.
verses.9:15: Therefore King Solomon made two hundred golden spears from a sum of six hundred gold pieces, which were spent on each spear;
verses.9:16: three hundred golden shields also, of three hundred gold pieces, with which each shield was covered; and the king placed them in the armory, which was planted with a grove.
verses.9:17: The king also made a great ivory throne, and clothed it with the purest gold;
verses.9:18: six steps also, by which one ascended to the throne, and a golden footstool, and two armrests on either side, and two lions standing beside the armrests,
verses.9:19: and also twelve other small lions standing upon the six steps on each side; there was no such throne in all the kingdoms.
verses.9:20: All the vessels of the king's banquet also were of gold, and the vessels of the house of the forest of Lebanon were of the purest gold. For in those days silver was regarded as nothing.
verses.9:21: For the ships of the king went to Tarshish with the servants of Hiram once in three years, and they brought from there gold, and silver, and ivory, and apes, and peacocks.
verses.9:22: Therefore Solomon was magnified above all the kings of the earth for riches and glory.
verses.9:23: And all the kings of the lands longed to see the face of Solomon, so that they might hear the wisdom that God had put in his heart;
verses.9:24: and they brought him gifts—vessels of silver and of gold, and garments, and weapons, and spices, horses, and mules—each year.
verses.9:25: Solomon also had forty thousand horses in stables, and twelve thousand chariots and horsemen; and he stationed them in the cities for chariots, and where the king was in Jerusalem.
verses.9:26: He also exercised dominion over all the kings from the river Euphrates to the land of the Philistines, and to the borders of Egypt.
verses.9:27: And he provided as great an abundance of silver in Jerusalem as of stones, and as great a multitude of cedars as of the sycamores that grow in the plains.
verses.9:28: And horses were brought to him from Egypt and from all the regions.
verses.9:29: Now the rest of the works of Solomon, the first and the last, are written in the words of Nathan the prophet, and in the books of Ahijah the Shilonite, and also in the vision of Iddo the seer against Jeroboam the son of Nebat.
verses.9:30: And Solomon reigned in Jerusalem over all Israel for forty years.
verses.9:31: And he slept with his fathers, and they buried him in the city of David; and Rehoboam his son reigned in his place.
verses.10:1: Now Rehoboam set out for Shechem, for all Israel had gathered there to make him king.
verses.10:2: When Jeroboam the son of Nebat, who was in Egypt (for indeed he had fled there from before Solomon), had heard of this, he immediately returned.
verses.10:3: And they called him, and he came with all Israel; and they spoke to Rehoboam, saying,
verses.10:4: "Your father pressed us with a very harsh yoke; command lighter things than your father, who imposed a heavy servitude upon us, and lighten a little of the burden, so that we may serve you."
verses.10:5: And he said, "After three days, return to me." And when the people had departed,
verses.10:6: he took counsel with the elders who had stood before his father Solomon while he was still alive, saying, "What counsel do you give, that I may answer the people?"
verses.10:7: And they said to him, "If you please this people and soothe them with gentle words, they will serve you at all times."
verses.10:8: But he abandoned the counsel of the elders, and began to confer with the young men who had been brought up with him and were in his retinue.
verses.10:9: And he said to them, "What do you think? Or what should I answer this people, who said to me, 'Lighten the yoke that your father imposed upon us'?"
verses.10:10: But they answered as young men, and brought up with him in luxury, and said, "Thus you will speak to the people who said to you, 'Your father made our yoke heavy; you lighten it,' and thus you will answer them: 'My little finger is thicker than my father's loins.
verses.10:11: My father imposed a heavy yoke upon you, and I will add a greater weight; my father beat you with whips, but I will beat you with scorpions.'"
verses.10:12: Therefore Jeroboam and all the people came to Rehoboam on the third day, just as he had commanded them.
verses.10:13: And the king answered harsh things, having abandoned the counsel of the elders;
verses.10:14: and he spoke according to the will of the young men: "My father imposed a heavy yoke upon you, which I will make heavier; my father beat you with whips, but I will beat you with scorpions."
verses.10:15: And he did not yield to the pleas of the people; for it was the will of God that His word might be fulfilled, which He had spoken by the hand of Ahijah the Shilonite to Jeroboam the son of Nebat.
verses.10:16: Now all the people, as the king spoke harsher things, spoke thus to him: "We have no portion in David, nor inheritance in the son of Jesse. Return to your tents, Israel; and you, shepherd your own house, David." And Israel went away to their tents.
verses.10:17: But over the sons of Israel who dwelt in the cities of Judah, Rehoboam reigned.
verses.10:18: And King Rehoboam sent Adoram, who was over the tributes, and the sons of Israel stoned him, and he died; however, King Rehoboam hurried to mount the chariot and fled to Jerusalem.
verses.10:19: And Israel withdrew from the house of David, to this day.
verses.11:1: Now Rehoboam came to Jerusalem and assembled the entire house of Judah and Benjamin, one hundred eighty thousand chosen and fighting men, to fight against Israel and turn his kingdom back to himself.
verses.11:2: And the word of the Lord came to Shemaiah the man of God, saying,
verses.11:3: "Speak to Rehoboam the son of Solomon, king of Judah, and to all Israel who are in Judah and Benjamin:
verses.11:4: 'This is what the Lord says: You must not go up, nor fight against your brothers; let each one return to his own house, because this has been done by My will.'" When they heard the word of the Lord, they turned back and did not march against Jeroboam.
verses.11:5: Now Rehoboam lived in Jerusalem, and he built walled cities in Judah.
verses.11:6: He built up Bethlehem, Etam, and Tekoa,
verses.11:7: Beth-zur also, and Soco, and Adullam,
verses.11:8: as well as Gath, Mareshah, and Ziph,
verses.11:9: and also Adoraim, Lachish, and Azekah,
verses.11:10: Zorah also, Aijalon, and Hebron, which were in Judah and Benjamin, heavily fortified cities.
verses.11:11: And when he had enclosed them with walls, he placed commanders in them and storehouses of provisions, that is, of oil and wine.
verses.11:12: Moreover, in every single city he made an armory of shields and spears, and he strengthened them with the utmost care, and he ruled over Judah and Benjamin.
verses.11:13: Now the priests and the Levites who were in all Israel came to him from all their dwelling places,
verses.11:14: leaving their outlying lands and their possessions, and crossing over to Judah and Jerusalem, because Jeroboam and his descendants had cast them off so that they would not serve in the priesthood of the Lord.
verses.11:15: And he appointed for himself priests of the high places, and of the demons, and of the calves that he had made.
verses.11:16: And also from all the tribes of Israel, whoever had given their heart to seek the Lord God of Israel came to Jerusalem to sacrifice their offerings before the Lord God of their fathers.
verses.11:17: And they strengthened the kingdom of Judah and established Rehoboam the son of Solomon for three years, for they walked in the ways of David and Solomon for only three years.
verses.11:18: Now Rehoboam took as wife Mahalath the daughter of Jerimoth the son of David, and also Abihail the daughter of Eliab the son of Jesse,
verses.11:19: who bore him sons: Jeush, Shemariah, and Zaham.
verses.11:20: After her he also took Maacah the daughter of Absalom, who bore him Abijah, Attai, Ziza, and Shelomith.
verses.11:21: Now Rehoboam loved Maacah the daughter of Absalom above all his wives and concubines, for he had taken eighteen wives and sixty concubines, and he fathered twenty-eight sons and sixty daughters.
verses.11:22: And he appointed Abijah the son of Maacah at the head as leader over all his brothers, for he planned to make him king,
verses.11:23: because he was wiser and more powerful over all his sons, and in all the territories of Judah and Benjamin, and in all the walled cities; and he supplied them with abundant food, and sought many wives.
verses.12:1: And when the kingdom of Rehoboam had been strengthened and made firm, he abandoned the law of the Lord, and all Israel with him.
verses.12:2: Now in the fifth year of the reign of Rehoboam, Shishak king of Egypt went up against Jerusalem (because they had sinned against the Lord),
verses.12:3: with one thousand two hundred chariots and sixty thousand horsemen; and the multitude that had come with him out of Egypt was without number, namely Libyans, Troglodytes, and Ethiopians.
verses.12:4: And he captured the heavily fortified cities in Judah, and came all the way to Jerusalem.
verses.12:5: Then Shemaiah the prophet went in to Rehoboam and the leaders of Judah who had gathered in Jerusalem, fleeing from Shishak, and said to them, "This is what the Lord says: 'You have abandoned Me, and I have abandoned you in the hand of Shishak.'"
verses.12:6: And the leaders of Israel and the king were dismayed, and they said, "The Lord is just."
verses.12:7: And when the Lord saw that they had humbled themselves, the word of the Lord came to Shemaiah, saying, "Because they have humbled themselves, I will not destroy them, and I will give them a little help, and My wrath will not drip upon Jerusalem by the hand of Shishak.
verses.12:8: Nevertheless, they will serve him, so that they may know the difference between My service and the service of the kingdom of the lands."
verses.12:9: Therefore Shishak king of Egypt withdrew from Jerusalem, after taking away the treasures of the house of the Lord and of the house of the king; and he carried off everything with him, even the golden shields that Solomon had made,
verses.12:10: in place of which the king made bronze ones, and handed them over to the commanders of the shield-bearers who guarded the vestibule of the palace.
verses.12:11: And whenever the king entered the house of the Lord, the shield-bearers would come and carry them, and would bring them back again to their armory.
verses.12:12: Nevertheless, because they humbled themselves, the anger of the Lord turned away from them, and they were not completely destroyed, since good works were also found in Judah.
verses.12:13: Therefore King Rehoboam grew strong in Jerusalem and reigned; now he was forty-one years old when he began to reign, and he reigned seventeen years in Jerusalem, the city that the Lord chose to establish His name there, from all the tribes of Israel; and his mother's name was Naamah the Ammonitess.
verses.12:14: And he did evil, and did not prepare his heart to seek the Lord.
verses.12:15: Now the deeds of Rehoboam, the first and the last, are written in the books of Shemaiah the prophet and of Iddo the seer, and carefully set forth; and Rehoboam and Jeroboam fought against each other all their days.
verses.12:16: And Rehoboam slept with his fathers, and was buried in the city of David; and Abijah his son reigned in his place.
verses.13:1: In the eighteenth year of King Jeroboam, Abijah began to reign over Judah.
verses.13:2: He reigned three years in Jerusalem, and his mother's name was Micaiah the daughter of Uriel of Gibeah; and there was war between Abijah and Jeroboam.
verses.13:3: And when Abijah entered into battle and had very warlike men, even four hundred thousand chosen men, Jeroboam drew up a battle line opposite him of eight hundred thousand men, who were themselves also chosen and exceedingly valiant for battle.
verses.13:4: Then Abijah stood on Mount Semeron, which was in Ephraim, and said, "Listen, Jeroboam and all Israel!
verses.13:5: Do you not know that the Lord God of Israel gave the kingdom over Israel to David forever, to him and to his sons as a covenant of salt?
verses.13:6: Yet Jeroboam the son of Nebat, the servant of Solomon the son of David, rose up and rebelled against his master.
verses.13:7: And utterly worthless men and sons of Belial gathered to him, and they prevailed against Rehoboam the son of Solomon; now Rehoboam was inexperienced and fearful of heart, and could not resist them.
verses.13:8: Now therefore you say that you can resist the kingdom of the Lord, which He possesses through the sons of David, and you have a great multitude of people, as well as the golden calves that Jeroboam made for you as gods.
verses.13:9: And you have driven out the priests of the Lord, the sons of Aaron, and the Levites, and have made priests for yourselves like all the peoples of the lands; whoever comes and consecrates his hand with a bull from the herd and with seven rams becomes a priest of those who are not gods.
verses.13:10: But our Lord is God, whom we do not abandon, and priests from the sons of Aaron minister to the Lord, and the Levites are in their order;
verses.13:11: they also offer burnt offerings to the Lord every single day, morning and evening, and incense prepared according to the precepts of the law, and the loaves are set out on the purest table, and with us is the golden lampstand and its lamps, to be lit always at evening; for we keep the precepts of the Lord our God, whom you have abandoned.
verses.13:12: Therefore in our army God is the leader, and His priests, who sound the trumpets and resound against you. Sons of Israel, do not fight against the Lord God of your fathers, because it is not to your advantage."
verses.13:13: While he was speaking these things, Jeroboam was preparing an ambush from behind. And while he stood facing the enemy, he surrounded unsuspecting Judah with his army.
verses.13:14: And looking back, Judah saw that battle was pressing in from in front and from behind, and cried out to the Lord, and the priests began to sound the trumpets.
verses.13:15: And all the men of Judah raised a shout; and look, as they shouted, God terrified Jeroboam and all Israel who stood facing Abijah and Judah.
verses.13:16: And the sons of Israel fled from Judah, and God delivered them into their hand.
verses.13:17: Therefore Abijah and his people struck them with a great slaughter, and five hundred thousand valiant men of Israel fell wounded.
verses.13:18: And the sons of Israel were humbled at that time, and the sons of Judah grew exceedingly strong, because they had placed their hope in the Lord God of their fathers.
verses.13:19: Now Abijah pursued the fleeing Jeroboam and captured his cities: Bethel and its daughters, and Jeshanah with its daughters, and Ephron also and its daughters;
verses.13:20: and Jeroboam was no longer able to resist in the days of Abijah, and the Lord struck him, and he died.
verses.13:21: Therefore Abijah, with his rule strengthened, took fourteen wives, and he fathered twenty-two sons and sixteen daughters.
verses.13:22: Now the rest of the words of Abijah, and of his ways and his deeds, are written most carefully in the book of Iddo the prophet.
verses.13:23: And Abijah slept with his fathers, and they buried him in the city of David; and Asa his son reigned in his place, in whose days the land had rest for ten years.
verses.14:1: Now Asa did what was good and pleasing in the sight of his God, and he overturned the altars of foreign worship and the high places.
verses.14:2: And he shattered the statues and cut down the groves,
verses.14:3: and he commanded Judah to seek the Lord God of their fathers, and to carry out the law and all the commandments;
verses.14:4: and he removed from all the cities of Judah the altars and the shrines, and he reigned in peace.
verses.14:5: He also built fortified cities in Judah, because he was undisturbed, and no wars had arisen in his times, with the Lord granting peace.
verses.14:6: Now he said to Judah, "Let us build these cities, and surround them with walls, and strengthen them with towers, gates, and bars, while everything is quiet from wars, because we have sought the Lord God of our fathers, and He has given us peace all around." So they built, and there was no hindrance in building.
verses.14:7: Now Asa had in his army three hundred thousand from Judah who carried shields and spears, and from Benjamin two hundred eighty thousand shield-bearers and archers; all of these were very valiant men.
verses.14:8: Now Zerah the Ethiopian went out against them with his army of one million, and with three hundred chariots; and he came as far as Mareshah.
verses.14:9: Then Asa went forward to meet him and drew up the ranks for war in the valley of Zephathah, which is near Mareshah;
verses.14:10: and he called upon the Lord God and said, "Lord, there is no distinction at all with You whether You assist with few or with many. Help us, Lord our God, for having confidence in You and in Your name, we have come against this multitude. Lord, You are our God; may no man prevail against You."
verses.14:11: Therefore the Lord terrified the Ethiopians before Asa and Judah, and the Ethiopians fled.
verses.14:12: And Asa and the people who were with him pursued them as far as Gerar; and the Ethiopians fell to utter destruction, because they were crushed as the Lord struck them down and His army fought. So they carried off great spoils,
verses.14:13: and they struck all the cities around Gerar, for a great terror had seized them all; and they pillaged the cities and carried away much plunder.
verses.14:14: And destroying the sheepfolds as well, they carried off a countless multitude of livestock and camels, and returned to Jerusalem.
verses.15:1: Now Azariah the son of Oded, when the Spirit of God came upon him,
verses.15:2: went out to meet Asa and said to him, "Listen to me, Asa, and all Judah and Benjamin: the Lord is with you, because you have been with Him. If you seek Him, you will find Him; but if you abandon Him, He will abandon you.
verses.15:3: Now many days passed in Israel without the true God, and without a teaching priest, and without law.
verses.15:4: And when they turn back in their distress to the Lord God of Israel and seek Him, they will find Him.
verses.15:5: In that time there will be no peace for the one going out and the one coming in, but terrors on every side upon all the inhabitants of the lands;
verses.15:6: for nation has fought against nation, and city against city, because the Lord will throw them into turmoil in every distress.
verses.15:7: You, therefore, be strong, and do not let your hands grow slack, for there will be a reward for your work."
verses.15:8: When Asa had heard this, namely, the words and the prophecy of Azariah the son of Oded the prophet, he was strengthened, and he removed the idols from all the land of Judah and from Benjamin, and from the cities of Mount Ephraim that he had captured; and he dedicated the altar of the Lord that was before the portico of the Lord.
verses.15:9: And he gathered all Judah and Benjamin, and the newcomers with them from Ephraim, and from Manasseh, and from Simeon; for many had fled to him from Israel, seeing that the Lord his God was with him.
verses.15:10: And when they had come to Jerusalem in the third month, in the fifteenth year of the reign of Asa,
verses.15:11: they sacrificed to the Lord on that day, from the spoils and plunder that they had brought, seven hundred oxen and seven thousand rams.
verses.15:12: And he entered according to custom to confirm the covenant, that they would seek the Lord God of their fathers with their whole heart and with their whole soul.
verses.15:13: "And if anyone," he said, "does not seek the Lord God of Israel, let him die, from the least to the greatest, from man to woman."
verses.15:14: And they swore to the Lord with a loud voice, with joyful shouting, and with the blast of the trumpet, and with the sound of horns,
verses.15:15: all who were in Judah, with a curse; for they swore with all their heart, and with their whole will they sought Him and found Him; and the Lord granted them rest all around.
verses.15:16: Moreover, he also deposed Maacah, the mother of King Asa, from her august authority, because she had made an image of Priapus in a grove, and he crushed all of it, and smashing it into pieces, he burned it in the brook Kidron.
verses.15:17: However, the high places were left in Israel; nevertheless, the heart of Asa was perfect all his days,
verses.15:18: and those things that his father and he himself had vowed, he brought into the house of the Lord: silver and gold, and varied furnishings of vessels.
verses.15:19: And there was no war until the thirty-fifth year of the reign of Asa.
verses.16:1: Now in the thirty-sixth year of his reign, Baasha king of Israel went up against Judah and was surrounding Ramah with a wall, so that no one could safely go out and come in from the kingdom of Asa.
verses.16:2: Therefore Asa brought out silver and gold from the treasuries of the house of the Lord and from the treasuries of the king, and sent them to Ben-hadad king of Syria, who lived in Damascus, saying,
verses.16:3: "There is a covenant between me and you; my father and your father also had an accord. For this reason I have sent you silver and gold, so that, breaking the covenant that you have with Baasha king of Israel, you may make him withdraw from me."
verses.16:4: Upon learning this, Ben-hadad sent the commanders of his armies against the cities of Israel, and they struck Ijon, Dan, and Abel-maim, and all the walled cities of Naphtali.
verses.16:5: When Baasha heard this, he stopped building Ramah and discontinued his work.
verses.16:6: Then King Asa took all Judah, and they carried off the stones from Ramah and the timber that Baasha had prepared for the building, and with them he built Geba and Mizpah.
verses.16:7: In that time Hanani the prophet came to Asa king of Judah and said to him, "Because you had confidence in the king of Syria, and not in the Lord your God, for that reason the army of the king of Syria has escaped from your hand.
verses.16:8: Were not the Ethiopians and the Libyans far more numerous, with chariots, horsemen, and an immense multitude, whom He delivered into your hand when you trusted in the Lord?
verses.16:9: For the eyes of the Lord survey the whole earth, and provide strength to those who believe in Him with a perfect heart. Therefore you have acted foolishly, and because of this, from the present time wars will rise up against you."
verses.16:10: And Asa, angry with the seer, ordered him to be put in the stocks, for he had become deeply indignant over this; and he killed very many of the people in that time.
verses.16:11: Now the deeds of Asa, first and last, are written in the book of the kings of Judah and Israel.
verses.16:12: Asa also fell ill in the thirty-ninth year of his reign with a most severe pain in his feet, and even in his illness he did not seek the Lord, but rather trusted in the skill of physicians.
verses.16:13: And he slept with his fathers, and died in the forty-first year of his reign.
verses.16:14: And they buried him in his tomb that he had dug for himself in the city of David; and they laid him upon his bed, filled with spices and prostitutes' ointments, which were compounded by the skill of perfumers, and they burned them over him with excessive pomp.
verses.17:1: Now Jehoshaphat his son reigned in his place, and he grew strong against Israel.
verses.17:2: And he stationed detachments of soldiers in all the cities of Judah that were surrounded with walls. And he positioned garrisons in the land of Judah and in the cities of Ephraim that Asa his father had captured.
verses.17:3: And the Lord was with Jehoshaphat, because he walked in the first ways of David his father, and did not hope in the Baals,
verses.17:4: but in the God of his father, and walked on in His commandments, and not according to the sins of Israel.
verses.17:5: And the Lord established the kingdom in his hand, and all Judah gave gifts to Jehoshaphat, and boundless wealth and much glory became his.
verses.17:6: And when his heart had taken courage on account of the ways of the Lord, he also removed the high places and the groves from Judah.
verses.17:7: Now in the third year of his reign he sent some of his leaders, Ben-hail, Obadiah, Zechariah, Nethanel, and Micaiah, to teach in the cities of Judah,
verses.17:8: and with them the Levites Shemaiah, Nethaniah, and Zebadiah, also Asahel, Shemiramoth, and Jonathan, and Adonijah, Tobijah, and Tob-adonijah, Levites, and with them Elishama and Jehoram, the priests;
verses.17:9: and they taught the people in Judah, having the book of the law of the Lord, and they went around all the cities of Judah and instructed the people.
verses.17:10: Therefore the dread of the Lord came upon all the kingdoms of the lands that were all around Judah, and they did not dare to wage war against Jehoshaphat.
verses.17:11: Moreover, the Philistines also brought gifts to Jehoshaphat and a tribute of silver; the Arabs also brought flocks, seven thousand seven hundred rams and just as many male goats.
verses.17:12: So Jehoshaphat grew and was magnified to the heights, and he built in Judah houses like towers and walled cities.
verses.17:13: And he prepared many works in the cities of Judah; fighting and mighty men were also in Jerusalem,
verses.17:14: whose number by the houses and families of each was this: in Judah, the leaders of the army, Adnah the commander, and with him three hundred thousand very mighty men.
verses.17:15: After him, Johanan the leader, and with him two hundred eighty thousand.
verses.17:16: After him also, Amasiah the son of Zichri, consecrated to the Lord, and with him two hundred thousand valiant men.
verses.17:17: Eliada, mighty for battle, followed him, and with him two hundred thousand of those holding bow and shield.
verses.17:18: After him also, Jehozabad, and with him one hundred eighty thousand equipped soldiers.
verses.17:19: All these were at the hand of the king, apart from the others whom he had placed in the walled cities throughout all Judah.
verses.18:1: So Jehoshaphat was very wealthy and renowned, and he was joined by marriage alliance to Ahab.
verses.18:2: And after some years he went down to him in Samaria. At his arrival, Ahab slaughtered very many rams and oxen for him and for the people who had come with him, and he persuaded him to go up to Ramoth-gilead.
verses.18:3: And Ahab king of Israel said to Jehoshaphat king of Judah, "Come with me to Ramoth-gilead." And he answered him, "As I am, so are you; as your people are, so also are my people; and we will be with you in the war."
verses.18:4: And Jehoshaphat said to the king of Israel, "Consult, I ask you, the word of the Lord right now."
verses.18:5: Therefore the king of Israel gathered four hundred men of the prophets and said to them, "Should we go to Ramoth-gilead to wage war, or refrain?" And they said, "Go up, and God will deliver it into the hand of the king."
verses.18:6: And Jehoshaphat said, "Is there not a prophet of the Lord here, so that we may inquire of him also?"
verses.18:7: And the king of Israel said to Jehoshaphat, "There is one man from whom we can seek the will of the Lord, but I hate him, because he does not prophesy good for me, but evil at all times; he is Micaiah the son of Imlah." And Jehoshaphat said, "Do not speak in this way, king."
verses.18:8: So the king of Israel called one of the eunuchs and said to him, "Call Micaiah the son of Imlah quickly."
verses.18:9: Now the king of Israel and Jehoshaphat king of Judah were each sitting on his throne, clothed in royal attire; and they were sitting on the threshing floor beside the gate of Samaria, and all the prophets were prophesying before them.
verses.18:10: And Zedekiah the son of Chenaanah made iron horns for himself and said, "This is what the Lord says: 'With these you will toss Syria until you crush it.'"
verses.18:11: And all the prophets were prophesying in the same way and saying, "Go up to Ramoth-gilead, and you will prosper, and the Lord will deliver them into the hand of the king."
verses.18:12: Now the messenger who had gone to call Micaiah said to him, "Look, the words of all the prophets with one mouth announce good things to the king; therefore I ask you that your word also not disagree with them, and that you speak favorable things."
verses.18:13: Micaiah answered him, "As the Lord lives, whatever my God says to me, this I will speak."
verses.18:14: So he came to the king. And the king said to him, "Micaiah, should we go to Ramoth-gilead to wage war, or refrain?" And he answered him, "Go up, for all things will turn out favorably, and the enemies will be delivered into your hands."
verses.18:15: And the king said, "Again and again I adjure you to speak to me nothing except what is true in the name of the Lord."
verses.18:16: And he said, "I saw all Israel scattered on the mountains, like sheep without a shepherd; and the Lord said, 'These have no masters; let each one return to his own house in peace.'"
verses.18:17: And the king of Israel said to Jehoshaphat, "Did I not tell you that this man would not prophesy anything good for me, but the things that are evil?"
verses.18:18: And he said, "Therefore hear the word of the Lord: I saw the Lord sitting on His throne, and all the host of heaven standing beside Him on the right and on the left.
verses.18:19: And the Lord said, 'Who will deceive Ahab king of Israel, so that he may go up and fall at Ramoth-gilead?' And while one spoke in this way and another in another,
verses.18:20: a spirit came forward and stood before the Lord and said, 'I will deceive him.' And the Lord said to him, 'By what means will you deceive him?'
verses.18:21: And he answered, 'I will go out and be a lying spirit in the mouth of all his prophets.' And the Lord said, 'You will deceive and prevail; go out and do so.'
verses.18:22: Now therefore, look, the Lord has put a spirit of lying in the mouth of all your prophets, and the Lord has spoken evil things concerning you."
verses.18:23: Then Zedekiah the son of Chenaanah approached and struck Micaiah's cheek and said, "By what way did the Spirit of the Lord pass from me to speak to you?"
verses.18:24: And Micaiah said, "You yourself will see on that day, when you enter chamber after chamber to hide yourself."
verses.18:25: Then the king of Israel commanded, saying, "Take Micaiah and lead him to Amon the ruler of the city and to Joash the son of Amelech.
verses.18:26: And you will say, 'This is what the king says: Put this man in prison, and give him a little bread and a very little water, until I return in peace.'"
verses.18:27: And Micaiah said, "If you return in peace, the Lord has not spoken in me." And he said, "Hear, all peoples."
verses.18:28: Therefore the king of Israel and Jehoshaphat king of Judah went up to Ramoth-gilead.
verses.18:29: And the king of Israel said to Jehoshaphat, "I will change my attire and go into battle in this way, but you put on your own garments." And having changed his attire, the king of Israel came to the war.
verses.18:30: Now the king of Syria had commanded the commanders of his cavalry, saying, "Do not fight against the smallest or against the greatest, except against the king of Israel alone."
verses.18:31: Therefore, when the leaders of the cavalry saw Jehoshaphat, they said, "This is the king of Israel." And they surrounded him, fighting; but he cried out to the Lord, and He helped him and turned them away from him.
verses.18:32: For when the commanders of the cavalry saw that he was not the king of Israel, they left him.
verses.18:33: Now it happened that one of the people shot an arrow at random and struck the king of Israel between the neck and the shoulder blades. And he said to his charioteer, "Turn your hand around and lead me out of the battle line, because I am wounded."
verses.18:34: And the battle came to an end on that day; moreover, the king of Israel stood in his chariot facing the Syrians until evening, and he died as the sun was setting.
verses.19:1: Now Jehoshaphat king of Judah returned to his own house peacefully in Jerusalem.
verses.19:2: Jehu the son of Hanani the seer met him and said to him, "You offer help to the wicked, and you are joined in friendship with those who hate the Lord, and therefore you indeed deserved the wrath of the Lord;
verses.19:3: but good works have been found in you, because you have removed the groves from the land of Judah and have prepared your heart to seek the Lord God of your fathers."
verses.19:4: So Jehoshaphat lived in Jerusalem, and he went out again to the people from Beersheba to Mount Ephraim, and he called them back to the Lord God of their fathers.
verses.19:5: And he appointed judges of the land in all the fortified cities of Judah, in each place,
verses.19:6: and charging the judges, he said, "See what you are doing, for you do not exercise the judgment of man, but of the Lord, and whatever you judge will come back upon you.
verses.19:7: Let the fear of the Lord be with you, and do all things with diligence; for with the Lord our God there is no injustice, nor partiality, nor desire for gifts."
verses.19:8: In Jerusalem also, Jehoshaphat appointed Levites, priests, and leaders of the families from Israel, to judge the judgment and the cause of the Lord for its inhabitants.
verses.19:9: And he commanded them, saying, "In this way you will act in the fear of the Lord, faithfully and with a perfect heart.
verses.19:10: Every case of your brothers who live in their cities that comes to you, between kindred and kindred, wherever there is a question concerning the law, concerning a commandment, concerning ceremonies, concerning ordinances, explain it to them, so that they may not sin against the Lord, and that wrath may not come upon you and upon your brothers; therefore, acting in this way, you will not sin.
verses.19:11: Now Amariah the priest and your high priest will preside over the matters that pertain to God; moreover, Zebadiah the son of Ishmael, who is the ruler in the house of Judah, will be over those affairs that pertain to the king's office; and you have the Levites as officers before you. Be strong and act diligently, and the Lord will be with you in good things."
verses.20:1: After these things, the sons of Moab and the sons of Ammon, and with them some of the Ammonites, gathered together against Jehoshaphat to fight against him.
verses.20:2: And messengers came and reported to Jehoshaphat, saying, "A great multitude has come against you from those places that are beyond the sea, and from Syria; and look, they are stationed in Hazazon-tamar, which is En-gedi."
verses.20:3: Now Jehoshaphat, terrified with fear, devoted himself wholly to petitioning the Lord, and he proclaimed a fast for all Judah.
verses.20:4: And Judah gathered together to implore the Lord; indeed, everyone from their cities also came to plead with Him.
verses.20:5: And when Jehoshaphat had taken his stand in the midst of the assembly of Judah and Jerusalem, in the house of the Lord before the new court,
verses.20:6: he said, "Lord God of our fathers, You are God in heaven, and You rule over all the kingdoms of the nations; in Your hand are strength and power, and no one can resist You.
verses.20:7: Did You not, our God, put to death all the inhabitants of this land before Your people Israel, and give it to the seed of Abraham Your friend forever?
verses.20:8: And they lived in it, and built in it a sanctuary for Your name, saying,
verses.20:9: 'If evils rush upon us, the sword of judgment, pestilence, and famine, we will stand before this house in Your sight, in which Your name has been invoked, and we will cry out to You in our distresses, and You will hear and save us.'
verses.20:10: Now therefore, look, the sons of Ammon, and Moab, and Mount Seir, through whom You did not allow Israel to pass when they were coming out of Egypt, but they turned aside from them and did not kill them,
verses.20:11: act to the contrary, and strive to drive us out of the possession that You handed over to us.
verses.20:12: Our God, will You not then judge them? Indeed, in us there is not strength great enough that we can resist this multitude that rushes upon us. But since we do not know what we ought to do, we have this alone remaining, to direct our eyes to You."
verses.20:13: And all Judah was standing before the Lord with their little ones, their wives, and their children.
verses.20:14: Now there was Jahaziel son of Zechariah, son of Benaiah, son of Jeiel, son of Mattaniah, a Levite of the sons of Asaph, upon whom the Spirit of the Lord came in the midst of the crowd,
verses.20:15: and he said, "Pay attention, all Judah, and you who live in Jerusalem, and you, King Jehoshaphat: This is what the Lord says to you: 'Do not be afraid, nor be terrified of this multitude, for the battle is not yours, but God's.
verses.20:16: Tomorrow you will go down against them; for they are about to go up by the ascent named Ziz, and you will find them at the top of the torrent that is opposite the wilderness of Jeruel.
verses.20:17: It will not be you who fight, but only stand confidently, and you will see the help of the Lord over you, Judah and Jerusalem. Do not be afraid, nor be terrified; tomorrow you will go out against them, and the Lord will be with you.'"
verses.20:18: Therefore Jehoshaphat, and Judah, and all the inhabitants of Jerusalem fell facedown to the ground before the Lord and worshiped Him.
verses.20:19: Moreover, the Levites of the sons of Kohath and of the sons of Korah were praising the Lord God of Israel with a loud voice on high.
verses.20:20: And when they had risen in the morning, they went out through the desert of Tekoa; and as they set out, Jehoshaphat, standing in their midst, said, "Hear me, men of Judah and all inhabitants of Jerusalem: believe in the Lord your God, and you will be secure; believe His prophets, and all things will turn out prosperously."
verses.20:21: And he gave counsel to the people, and appointed singers of the Lord to praise Him in their companies and to go before the army, and with harmonious voice to say, "Give praise to the Lord, for His mercy is forever."
verses.20:22: And when they had begun to sing praises, the Lord turned their ambushes against themselves, namely, those of the sons of Ammon, and Moab, and Mount Seir, who had gone out to fight against Judah; and they were struck down.
verses.20:23: For the sons of Ammon and Moab rose up together against the inhabitants of Mount Seir to kill and destroy them; and when they had carried this out in deed, turning against themselves as well, they fell by mutual wounds.
verses.20:24: Now when Judah had come to the lookout that faces the wilderness, they saw from afar the whole region far and wide full of corpses, and that no one survived who had been able to escape slaughter.
verses.20:25: Therefore Jehoshaphat, and all the people with him, came to strip the spoils of the dead; and they found among the corpses various goods, garments as well, and very precious vessels, and they plundered so that they could not carry everything, nor carry away the spoils over three days because of the vastness of the plunder.
verses.20:26: On the fourth day, however, they gathered together in the Valley of Blessing; for indeed, because they had blessed the Lord there, they called that place Valley of Blessing up to the present day.
verses.20:27: And every man of Judah, and the inhabitants of Jerusalem, and Jehoshaphat before them, returned to Jerusalem with great gladness, because the Lord had given them joy over their enemies.
verses.20:28: And they entered into Jerusalem with harps, and lyres, and trumpets, into the house of the Lord.
verses.20:29: And the dread of the Lord fell upon all the kingdoms of the lands when they heard that the Lord had fought against the enemies of Israel.
verses.20:30: And the kingdom of Jehoshaphat was at rest, and God granted him peace all around.
verses.20:31: So Jehoshaphat reigned over Judah, and he was thirty-five years old when he began to reign; and he reigned twenty-five years in Jerusalem, and the name of his mother was Azubah daughter of Shilhi.
verses.20:32: And he walked in the way of his father Asa, and did not turn aside from it, doing what was pleasing before the Lord.
verses.20:33: Nevertheless, he did not remove the high places, and the people had not yet directed their heart to the Lord God of their fathers.
verses.20:34: Now the rest of the deeds of Jehoshaphat, first and last, are written in the words of Jehu son of Hanani, which he arranged in the books of the kings of Israel.
verses.20:35: After these things, Jehoshaphat king of Judah entered into friendship with Ahaziah king of Israel, whose works were most wicked.
verses.20:36: And he became a partner in making ships that would go to Tarshish, and they made a fleet in Ezion-geber.
verses.20:37: Then Eliezer son of Dodavahu, from Mareshah, prophesied to Jehoshaphat, saying, "Because you have had an alliance with Ahaziah, the Lord has struck your works." And the ships were shattered, and they could not go to Tarshish.
verses.21:1: Now Jehoshaphat slept with his fathers, and he was buried with them in the city of David; and his son Jehoram reigned in his place.
verses.21:2: He had brothers, sons of Jehoshaphat: Azariah, and Jehiel, and Zechariah, and Azariah, and Michael, and Shephatiah; all these were sons of Jehoshaphat king of Judah.
verses.21:3: And their father gave them many gifts of silver and gold, and revenues, along with very strongly fortified cities in Judah; but the kingdom he handed over to Jehoram, because he was the firstborn.
verses.21:4: Therefore Jehoram rose up over the kingdom of his father; and when he had established himself, he killed all his brothers with the sword, and some of the princes of Israel as well.
verses.21:5: Jehoram was thirty-two years old when he began to reign, and he reigned eight years in Jerusalem.
verses.21:6: And he walked in the ways of the kings of Israel, just as the house of Ahab had done, for the daughter of Ahab was his wife; and he did evil in the sight of the Lord.
verses.21:7: Yet the Lord was unwilling to destroy the house of David because of the covenant that He had entered into with him, and because He had promised to give a lamp to him and to his sons at all times.
verses.21:8: In those days Edom rebelled so as not to be subject to Judah, and appointed a king for itself.
verses.21:9: And when Jehoram had crossed over with his princes and all the cavalry that was with him, he rose up by night and struck Edom, which had surrounded him, and all the commanders of its cavalry.
verses.21:10: Nevertheless, Edom rebelled so as not to be under the dominion of Judah up to this day; at that time Libnah also withdrew so as not to be under his hand. For he had abandoned the Lord God of his fathers;
verses.21:11: moreover, he also built high places in the cities of Judah, and caused the inhabitants of Jerusalem to commit fornication, and Judah to transgress.
verses.21:12: And a letter was brought to him from Elijah the prophet, in which it was written, "This is what the Lord God of your father David says: 'Because you have not walked in the ways of your father Jehoshaphat, and in the ways of Asa king of Judah,
verses.21:13: but have proceeded along the path of the kings of Israel, and have caused Judah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem to commit fornication, imitating the fornication of the house of Ahab, and furthermore have also killed your brothers, the house of your father, who were better than you,
verses.21:14: look, the Lord will strike you with a great blow, along with your people, and your sons, and your wives, and all your possessions.
verses.21:15: And you yourself will be sick with a most grievous illness of your abdomen, until your vital organs come out little by little, day by day.'"
verses.21:16: Therefore the Lord stirred up against Jehoram the spirit of the Philistines and of the Arabs who border on the Ethiopians;
verses.21:17: and they went up into the land of Judah and devastated it, and plundered all the possessions that were found in the king's house, and moreover his sons and his wives; and no son remained to him except Jehoahaz, who was the youngest.
verses.21:18: And over and above all these things, the Lord struck him with an incurable illness of the bowels.
verses.21:19: And as day succeeded day, and the spans of time rolled on, the cycle of two years was completed; and thus, consumed by a long wasting, so that he even discharged his own intestines, he lost both his illness and his life together. And he died in a most grievous sickness, and the people did not perform funeral rites for him according to the custom of burning, as they had done for his ancestors.
verses.21:20: He was thirty-two years old when he began to reign, and he reigned eight years in Jerusalem. And he did not walk rightly, and they buried him in the city of David, though not in the tomb of the kings.
verses.22:1: Then the inhabitants of Jerusalem appointed his youngest son Ahaziah king in his place; for the raiders of the Arabs who had rushed into the camp had killed all the older ones who had been before him; and Ahaziah son of Jehoram king of Judah reigned.
verses.22:2: Ahaziah was forty-two years old when he began to reign, and he reigned one year in Jerusalem; and the name of his mother was Athaliah daughter of Omri.
verses.22:3: He also walked along the ways of the house of Ahab, for his mother incited him to act wickedly.
verses.22:4: Therefore he did evil in the sight of the Lord, like the house of Ahab; for they themselves were his counselors after the death of his father, to his destruction;
