verses.22:5: and he walked in their counsels. And he went with Jehoram son of Ahab, king of Israel, to war against Hazael king of Syria at Ramoth-gilead; and the Syrians wounded Jehoram.
verses.22:6: He returned to be healed in Jezreel, for he had received many wounds in the aforementioned battle. Therefore Ahaziah son of Jehoram, king of Judah, went down to visit Jehoram son of Ahab in Jezreel, who was sick.
verses.22:7: For it was the will of God against Ahaziah that he should come to Jehoram, and that when he had come, he should also go out with him against Jehu son of Nimshi, whom the Lord anointed to destroy the house of Ahab.
verses.22:8: Therefore, while Jehu was overthrowing the house of Ahab, he found the princes of Judah and the sons of Ahaziah's brothers, who were serving him, and he killed them.
verses.22:9: Searching for Ahaziah himself as well, he captured him hiding in Samaria; and when he had been brought to him, he killed him; and they buried him, because he was the son of Jehoshaphat, who had sought the Lord with all his heart. And there was no longer any hope that anyone from the lineage of Ahaziah would reign.
verses.22:10: For indeed, his mother Athaliah, seeing that her son was dead, rose up and killed all the royal lineage of the house of Jehoram.
verses.22:11: But Jehoshabeath, the daughter of the king, took Joash son of Ahaziah, and stole him away from the midst of the king's sons while they were being killed, and hid him with his nurse in the chamber of the beds; now Jehoshabeath, who had hidden him, was the daughter of King Jehoram, the wife of Jehoiada the high priest, and the sister of Ahaziah; and for that reason Athaliah did not kill him.
verses.22:12: So he was hidden with them in the house of God for six years, during which Athaliah reigned over the land.
verses.23:1: Now in the seventh year, Jehoiada strengthened himself and took the centurions, namely Azariah son of Jeroham, and Ishmael son of Jehohanan, also Azariah son of Obed, and Maaseiah son of Adaiah, and Elishaphat son of Zichri; and he entered into a covenant with them.
verses.23:2: Going around Judah, they gathered the Levites from all the cities of Judah and the leaders of the families of Israel, and they came to Jerusalem.
verses.23:3: So the whole multitude entered into a pact in the house of God with the king, and Jehoiada said to them, "Look, the son of the king will reign, just as the Lord spoke concerning the sons of David.
verses.23:4: This, therefore, is the thing that you will do:
verses.23:5: a third part of you who come for the Sabbath, of the priests, and of the Levites, and of the gatekeepers, will be at the gates; and a third part at the house of the king; and a third at the gate that is called the Gate of the Foundation; but let all the rest of the common people be in the courts of the house of the Lord.
verses.23:6: And let no one else enter the house of the Lord, except the priests and those of the Levites who minister; let them alone enter, because they are consecrated, and let all the rest of the common people keep the watches of the Lord.
verses.23:7: Now let the Levites surround the king, each one having his weapons (and if anyone else enters the temple, let him be put to death), and let them be with the king both when he goes in and when he goes out."
verses.23:8: So the Levites and all Judah did according to all that Jehoiada the high priest had commanded; and each one took the men who were under him and were coming in the order of the Sabbath, along with those who had completed the Sabbath and were about to go out, since Jehoiada the high priest had not let the companies depart that were accustomed to succeed one another week by week.
verses.23:9: And Jehoiada the priest gave to the centurions the spears, shields, and bucklers of King David, which he had consecrated in the house of the Lord.
verses.23:10: And he stationed all the people, holding daggers, from the right side of the temple to the left side of the temple, before the altar and the temple, all around the king.
verses.23:11: And they brought out the king's son, and placed upon him the diadem and the testimony, and gave the law into his hand to hold, and made him king; Jehoiada the high priest and his sons also anointed him, and they invoked blessings upon him and said, "May the king live!"
verses.23:12: When Athaliah heard this, namely the sound of those running and praising the king, she went in to the people in the temple of the Lord.
verses.23:13: And when she saw the king standing upon the step at the entrance, and the leaders and the companies around him, and all the people of the land rejoicing and sounding trumpets and playing together on instruments of various kinds, and the sound of those praising, she tore her garments and said, "Conspiracy! Conspiracy!"
verses.23:14: Then Jehoiada the high priest went out to the centurions and the leaders of the army and said to them, "Bring her out beyond the precincts of the temple, and let her be put to death outside by the sword." And the priest commanded that she not be killed in the house of the Lord,
verses.23:15: and they laid hands on her neck; and when she had entered the Horse Gate of the house of the king, they put her to death there.
verses.23:16: Then Jehoiada made a covenant between himself, and all the people, and the king, that they would be the people of the Lord.
verses.23:17: And so all the people entered the house of Baal and destroyed it, and smashed its altars and images; they also put Mattan, the priest of Baal, to death before the altars.
verses.23:18: Now Jehoiada appointed overseers in the house of the Lord under the hands of the priests and the Levites, whom David had distributed in the house of the Lord, to offer burnt offerings to the Lord, as it is written in the law of Moses, with joy and songs, according to the arrangement of David.
verses.23:19: He also appointed gatekeepers at the gates of the house of the Lord, so that no one unclean in any matter should enter it.
verses.23:20: And he took the centurions, and the mightiest men, and the leaders of the people, and all the common people of the land, and they brought the king down from the house of the Lord and had him enter through the middle of the Upper Gate into the house of the king, and they seated him on the royal throne.
verses.23:21: And all the people of the land rejoiced, and the city was quiet; but Athaliah was put to death by the sword.
verses.24:1: Joash was seven years old when he began to reign, and he reigned forty years in Jerusalem; the name of his mother was Zibiah of Beersheba.
verses.24:2: And he did what is good before the Lord all the days of Jehoiada the priest.
verses.24:3: Now Jehoiada took two wives for him, by whom he fathered sons and daughters.
verses.24:4: After these things, it pleased Joash to restore the house of the Lord.
verses.24:5: And he gathered the priests and the Levites and said to them, "Go out to the cities of Judah, and collect money from all Israel for the repairs of the temple of your God year by year, and do this quickly." However, the Levites acted rather negligently.
verses.24:6: So the king summoned Jehoiada the chief and said to him, "Why did you not take care to compel the Levites to bring in from Judah and from Jerusalem the money that was decreed by Moses, the servant of the Lord, that the whole multitude of Israel should bring it into the tabernacle of the testimony?"
verses.24:7: For the most wicked Athaliah and her sons destroyed the house of God, and with all the things that had been consecrated in the temple of the Lord they adorned the shrine of the Baals.
verses.24:8: Therefore the king commanded, and they made a chest and placed it beside the gate of the house of the Lord, on the outside.
verses.24:9: And it was proclaimed in Judah and Jerusalem that each one should bring to the Lord the payment that Moses, the servant of God, decreed upon all Israel in the wilderness.
verses.24:10: And all the leaders and all the people rejoiced; and entering, they brought it into the chest of the Lord and put it in so that it was filled.
verses.24:11: And whenever it was time to bring the chest before the king by the hands of the Levites (for they saw much money), the king's scribe and the one whom the chief priest had appointed would come in and pour out the money that was in the chest, while they carried the chest back to its place; and thus they did day by day. And a vast amount of money was gathered,
verses.24:12: which the king and Jehoiada gave to those who were in charge of the works of the house of the Lord; and they hired with it stonecutters and craftsmen of every kind of work to restore the house of the Lord, and also smiths of iron and bronze, so that what had begun to fall might be shored up.
verses.24:13: And those who were working acted diligently, and the scar of the walls was closed over by their hands; and they raised up the house of the Lord to its former state and made it stand firmly.
verses.24:14: And when they had completed all the works, they brought the remaining part of the money before the king and Jehoiada, from which were made vessels of the temple for the service and for burnt offerings, bowls also, and other vessels of gold and silver; burnt offerings were offered in the house of the Lord continually all the days of Jehoiada.
verses.24:15: Now Jehoiada grew old, full of days, and he died when he was one hundred thirty years old;
verses.24:16: and they buried him in the city of David with the kings, because he had done good toward Israel and toward his house.
verses.24:17: Now after Jehoiada died, the leaders of Judah came in and bowed down to the king; and he, charmed by their deference, yielded to them.
verses.24:18: And they abandoned the temple of the Lord God of their fathers, and served sacred groves and carved images; and wrath came against Judah and Jerusalem because of this sin.
verses.24:19: And He kept sending prophets to them so that they might return to the Lord, yet they refused to listen to them testifying.
verses.24:20: Then the Spirit of God clothed Zechariah the priest, son of Jehoiada, and he stood in the sight of the people and said to them, "This is what the Lord God says: 'Why do you transgress the command of the Lord, which will not profit you, and why have you abandoned the Lord, so that He has abandoned you?'"
verses.24:21: And gathering together against him, they threw stones according to the king's command in the court of the house of the Lord.
verses.24:22: And King Joash did not remember the mercy that Jehoiada, his father, had shown to him, but he put his son to death. And as he was dying, he said, "May the Lord see and require it."
verses.24:23: And when a year had elapsed, the army of Syria went up against him, and came into Judah and Jerusalem, and put all the leaders of the people to death, and they sent all the plunder to the king in Damascus.
verses.24:24: And indeed, although a very small number of Syrians had come, the Lord delivered a vast multitude into their hands, because they had abandoned the Lord God of their fathers; upon Joash also they executed shameful judgments.
verses.24:25: And departing, they left him in severe illnesses; then his own servants rose up against him in vengeance for the blood of the son of Jehoiada the priest, and killed him on his bed, and he died; and they buried him in the city of David, but not in the tombs of the kings.
verses.24:26: Now those who conspired against him were Zabad son of Shimeath the Ammonitess, and Jehozabad son of Shimrith the Moabitess.
verses.24:27: Now his sons, and the sum of money that had been gathered together under him, and the restoration of the house of God are written more carefully in the book of the kings; and his son Amaziah reigned in his place.
verses.25:1: Amaziah was twenty-five years old when he began to reign, and he reigned for twenty-nine years in Jerusalem; his mother's name was Jehoaddan from Jerusalem.
verses.25:2: And he did good in the sight of the Lord, yet not with a complete heart.
verses.25:3: And when he saw that his rule had been strengthened for him, he executed the servants who had killed the king, his father.
verses.25:4: But he did not put their sons to death, just as it is written in the book of the law of Moses, where the Lord commanded, saying, "Fathers will not be killed for sons, nor sons for their fathers, but each one will die in his own sin."
verses.25:5: Therefore Amaziah assembled Judah and organized them by families, with tribunes and centurions throughout all Judah and Benjamin; and he mustered them from twenty years old and upward, and found three hundred thousand young men who could go out to battle and hold spear and shield.
verses.25:6: He also hired one hundred thousand strong men from Israel for one hundred talents of silver.
verses.25:7: Now a man of God came to him and said, "King, do not let the army of Israel go out with you, for the Lord is not with Israel and all the sons of Ephraim.
verses.25:8: But if you think that wars depend on the strength of an army, God will cause you to be overcome by enemies; for it belongs to God both to help and to put to flight."
verses.25:9: And Amaziah said to the man of God, "What then will become of the one hundred talents that I gave to the soldiers of Israel?" And the man of God answered him, "The Lord has the means from which He can give you much more than these."
verses.25:10: So Amaziah separated the army that had come to him from Ephraim, so that it would return to its own place; yet they, fiercely angry against Judah, returned to their own region.
verses.25:11: Then Amaziah confidently led out his people and went to the Valley of Salt, and struck down ten thousand of the sons of Seir.
verses.25:12: And the sons of Judah captured another ten thousand men and brought them to the cliff of a certain rock, and hurled them headlong from the summit; and all of them burst apart.
verses.25:13: But that army which Amaziah had sent back so that it would not go with him to battle spread out through the cities of Judah, from Samaria as far as Beth-horon, and after putting three thousand to death, seized great plunder.
verses.25:14: Now Amaziah, after the slaughter of the Edomites and after bringing the gods of the sons of Seir, set them up as gods for himself, and worshiped them, and burned incense to them.
verses.25:15: For this reason the Lord, angry against Amaziah, sent a prophet to him to say to him, "Why have you worshiped gods who did not deliver their own people from your hand?"
verses.25:16: And while he was speaking these things, he answered him, "Are you a counselor of the king? Stop, so that I do not put you to death." "I know," the prophet said as he departed, "that God has planned to kill you, because you have done this evil and, moreover, have not consented to my counsel."
verses.25:17: Therefore Amaziah king of Judah, having taken very bad counsel, sent to Joash son of Jehoahaz, son of Jehu, king of Israel, saying, "Come, let us see one another."
verses.25:18: But he sent back messengers, saying, "The thistle that is in Lebanon sent to the cedar of Lebanon, saying, 'Give your daughter to my son as a wife.' And look, the wild beasts that were in the forest of Lebanon passed by and trampled the thistle.
verses.25:19: You have said, 'I struck down Edom,' and therefore your heart is lifted up in pride. Stay in your house; why do you provoke disaster against yourself, so that both you and Judah with you fall?"
verses.25:20: Amaziah refused to listen, because it was the will of the Lord that he should be handed over into the hands of enemies because of the gods of Edom.
verses.25:21: Therefore Joash king of Israel went up, and they faced one another; now Amaziah king of Judah was in Beth-shemesh of Judah.
verses.25:22: And Judah fell before Israel and fled to their tents.
verses.25:23: Then Joash king of Israel captured Amaziah king of Judah, son of Joash, son of Jehoahaz, in Beth-shemesh and brought him to Jerusalem; and he tore down its wall from the Ephraim Gate to the Corner Gate, four hundred cubits.
verses.25:24: He also brought back to Samaria all the gold and silver, and all the vessels that he had found in the house of God and with Obed-edom, and also in the treasuries of the royal house, as well as the sons of the hostages.
verses.25:25: Now Amaziah son of Joash, king of Judah, lived fifteen years after Joash son of Jehoahaz, king of Israel, died.
verses.25:26: Now the rest of the accounts of Amaziah, first and last, are written in the book of the kings of Judah and Israel.
verses.25:27: And after he turned away from the Lord, they laid a plot against him in Jerusalem. And when he had fled to Lachish, they sent and put him to death there.
verses.25:28: And carrying him back on horses, they buried him with his fathers in the city of David.
verses.26:1: Now all the people of Judah made his son Uzziah, sixteen years old, king in place of Amaziah his father.
verses.26:2: He himself built Elath and restored it to the dominion of Judah, after the king slept with his fathers.
verses.26:3: Uzziah was sixteen years old when he began to reign, and he reigned for fifty-two years in Jerusalem; his mother's name was Jecoliah from Jerusalem.
verses.26:4: And he did what was right in the eyes of the Lord, according to all that Amaziah his father had done.
verses.26:5: And he sought out the Lord in the days of Zechariah, who understood and saw God; and while he sought the Lord, He directed him in all things.
verses.26:6: Then he went out and fought against the Philistines, and tore down the wall of Gath, and the wall of Jabneh, and the wall of Ashdod; he also built towns in Ashdod and among the Philistines.
verses.26:7: And God helped him against the Philistines, and against the Arabs who lived in Gur-baal, and against the Ammonites.
verses.26:8: And the Ammonites weighed out gifts to Uzziah, and his name became widely known as far as the entrance of Egypt because of his frequent victories.
verses.26:9: And Uzziah built towers in Jerusalem over the Corner Gate and over the Valley Gate, and others on the same side of the wall, and fortified them.
verses.26:10: He also constructed towers in the wilderness and dug very many cisterns, because he had much livestock both in the plains and in the vastness of the desert; he also had vineyards and vinedressers in the mountains and in Carmel, for he was a man devoted to agriculture.
verses.26:11: Now there was an army of his warriors who marched out to battles under the hand of Jeiel the scribe and Maaseiah the teacher, and under the hand of Hananiah, who was one of the king's commanders.
verses.26:12: And the entire number of the leaders by families, valiant men, was two thousand six hundred.
verses.26:13: And under them was the entire army of three hundred and seven thousand five hundred, who were fit for wars and fought for the king against adversaries.
verses.26:14: Uzziah also prepared for them, that is, for the whole army, shields, and spears, and helmets, and coats of mail, and bows and slings for hurling stones.
verses.26:15: And he made in Jerusalem machines of various kinds, which he placed on the towers and on the corners of the walls to launch arrows and large stones. And his name went out far, because the Lord was helping him and had strengthened him.
verses.26:16: But when he had been strengthened, his heart was lifted up to his own ruin, and he neglected the Lord his God; and entering the temple of the Lord, he wanted to burn incense on the altar of incense.
verses.26:17: And immediately Azariah the priest, having entered after him, and with him eighty priests of the Lord, very valiant men,
verses.26:18: resisted the king and said, "It is not your office, Uzziah, to burn incense to the Lord, but that of the priests, that is, the sons of Aaron, who have been consecrated for this kind of ministry. Go out from the sanctuary; do not show contempt, because this will not be credited to you for glory by the Lord God."
verses.26:19: And Uzziah became angry, and holding a censer in his hand to burn incense, he threatened the priests. And immediately leprosy broke out on his forehead before the priests, in the house of the Lord, by the altar of incense.
verses.26:20: And when Azariah the high priest and all the other priests looked at him, they saw the leprosy on his forehead and hastily drove him out. Indeed, he himself, terrified, hurried to go out, because he had immediately felt the stroke of the Lord.
verses.26:21: Therefore King Uzziah was a leper until the day of his death, and he lived in a separate house, full of leprosy, because of which he had been cast out from the house of the Lord. Meanwhile, Jotham his son governed the king's house and judged the people of the land.
verses.26:22: Now Isaiah son of Amoz, the prophet, wrote the rest of the accounts of Uzziah, first and last.
verses.26:23: And Uzziah slept with his fathers, and they buried him in the field of the royal tombs because he was a leper; and Jotham his son reigned in his place.
verses.27:1: Jotham was twenty-five years old when he began to reign, and he reigned for sixteen years in Jerusalem; his mother's name was Jerushah, daughter of Zadok.
verses.27:2: And he did what was right before the Lord, according to all that Uzziah his father had done, except that he did not enter the temple of the Lord; and the people were still sinning.
verses.27:3: He himself built the high gate of the house of the Lord, and he constructed many things on the wall of Ophel.
verses.27:4: He also built cities in the mountains of Judah, and fortresses and towers in the forests.
verses.27:5: He himself fought against the king of the sons of Ammon and defeated them, and at that time the sons of Ammon gave him one hundred talents of silver, and ten thousand kors of wheat, and just as many kors of barley; the sons of Ammon supplied these things to him in the second and third year.
verses.27:6: And Jotham was strengthened, because he had directed his ways before the Lord his God.
verses.27:7: Now the rest of the accounts of Jotham, and all his battles and works, are written in the book of the kings of Israel and Judah.
verses.27:9: And Jotham slept with his fathers, and they buried him in the city of David; and Ahaz his son reigned in his place.
verses.28:1: Ahaz was twenty years old when he began to reign, and he reigned sixteen years in Jerusalem. He did not do what was right in the sight of the Lord like David his father,
verses.28:2: but walked in the ways of the kings of Israel, and moreover cast statues for the Baals.
verses.28:3: He is the one who burned incense in the valley of Ben-hinnom, and purified his sons in fire according to the rite of the nations whom the Lord killed at the arrival of the sons of Israel.
verses.28:4: He also sacrificed and kindled incense on the high places, and on the hills, and under every leafy tree.
verses.28:5: And the Lord his God delivered him into the hand of the king of Syria, who struck him and took great plunder from his realm and brought it to Damascus; he was also delivered into the hands of the king of Israel and struck with a great blow.
verses.28:6: And Pekah son of Remaliah killed one hundred twenty thousand from Judah in one day, all fighting men, because they had abandoned the Lord God of their fathers.
verses.28:7: At the same time Zichri, a mighty man from Ephraim, killed Maaseiah the king's son, and Azrikam the leader of his house, and also Elkanah, second after the king.
verses.28:8: And the sons of Israel captured from their brothers two hundred thousand women, boys, and girls, and boundless plunder, and carried it into Samaria.
verses.28:9: At that time a prophet of the Lord, named Oded, was there, who went out to meet the army coming to Samaria and said to them, "Look, the Lord God of your fathers, angry against Judah, delivered them into your hands, and you killed them savagely, so that your cruelty reached up to heaven.
verses.28:10: Moreover, you want to subjugate the sons of Judah and Jerusalem for yourselves as male and female slaves, which by no means needs to be done, for you have sinned in this against the Lord your God.
verses.28:11: But listen to my counsel, and lead back the captives whom you have brought from your brothers, for the great wrath of the Lord hangs over you."
verses.28:12: Therefore men from the leaders of the sons of Ephraim, Azariah son of Johanan, Berechiah son of Meshillemoth, Hezekiah son of Shallum, and Amasa son of Hadlai, stood up against those who were coming from the battle,
verses.28:13: and said to them, "You will not bring the captives in here, so that we do not sin against the Lord. Why do you want to add to our sins and heap up old offenses? For it is a great sin, and the anger of the wrath of the Lord hangs over Israel."
verses.28:14: And the fighting men left the plunder and everything that they had captured before the leaders and the entire multitude.
verses.28:15: And the men whom we mentioned above stood up, and taking the captives, they clothed all who were naked from the spoils; and when they had clothed them, put sandals on them, refreshed them with food and drink, anointed them because of their weariness, and given them care, they placed all who could not walk and were weak in body on pack animals and brought them to Jericho, the city of palm trees, to their brothers; and they themselves returned to Samaria.
verses.28:16: At that time King Ahaz sent to the king of the Assyrians, asking for help.
verses.28:17: And the Edomites came and struck many from Judah, and took great plunder.
verses.28:18: The Philistines also spread out through the cities of the plain and toward the south of Judah, and they captured Beth-shemesh, Aijalon, and Gederoth, and also Soco, Timnah, and Gimzo, with their villages, and lived in them.
verses.28:19: For the Lord had humbled Judah because of Ahaz king of Judah, because he had stripped it of help and had held the Lord in contempt.
verses.28:20: And He brought against him Tiglath-pileser king of the Assyrians, who both afflicted him and devastated him with no one resisting.
verses.28:21: Therefore Ahaz, having plundered the house of the Lord and the house of the kings and leaders, gave gifts to the king of the Assyrians, and yet it was of no benefit to him.
verses.28:22: And moreover, in the time of his distress, he increased contempt toward the Lord, King Ahaz himself in person;
verses.28:23: he sacrificed victims to the gods of Damascus, who struck him, and said, "The gods of the kings of Syria help them; I will appease them with sacrifices, and they will stand by me," whereas on the contrary they were a ruin to him and to all Israel.
verses.28:24: Therefore, having seized and shattered all the vessels of the house of God, Ahaz shut the doors of the temple of God and made altars for himself in all the corners of Jerusalem.
verses.28:25: In all the cities of Judah also he built altars for burning incense, and provoked the Lord God of his fathers to anger.
verses.28:26: Now the rest of his words, and of all his deeds, first and last, are written in the book of the kings of Judah and Israel.
verses.28:27: And Ahaz slept with his fathers, and they buried him in the city of Jerusalem, for they did not receive him into the tombs of the kings of Israel. And Hezekiah his son reigned in his place.
verses.29:1: Therefore Hezekiah began to reign when he was twenty-five years old, and he reigned twenty-nine years in Jerusalem; his mother's name was Abijah, daughter of Zechariah.
verses.29:2: And he did what was pleasing in the sight of the Lord, according to all that David his father had done.
verses.29:3: He, in the first year and month of his reign, opened the doors of the house of the Lord and repaired them.
verses.29:4: And he brought in the priests and the Levites, and gathered them into the eastern square.
verses.29:5: And he said to them, "Listen to me, Levites, and sanctify yourselves; cleanse the house of the Lord God of your fathers, and remove all uncleanness from the sanctuary.
verses.29:6: Our fathers have sinned and done evil in the sight of the Lord our God, abandoning Him; they have turned their faces away from the tabernacle of the Lord and turned their backs.
verses.29:7: They shut the doors that were in the portico, and extinguished the lamps, and did not burn incense, and did not offer burnt offerings in the sanctuary to the God of Israel.
verses.29:8: Therefore the wrath of the Lord was aroused upon Judah and Jerusalem, and He delivered them over to turmoil, and to destruction, and to hissing, just as you yourselves see with your eyes.
verses.29:9: Look, our fathers have fallen by the sword; our sons, our daughters, and our wives have been led away captive because of this crime.
verses.29:10: Now therefore it pleases me that we enter into a covenant with the Lord God of Israel, and He will turn away from us the wrath of His anger.
verses.29:11: My sons, do not be negligent; the Lord has chosen you to stand before Him, and serve Him, and worship Him, and burn incense to Him."
verses.29:12: Therefore the Levites arose: Mahath son of Amasai, and Joel son of Azariah, of the sons of Kohath; and of the sons of Merari, Kish son of Abdi, and Azariah son of Jehallelel. And of the sons of Gershom, Joah son of Zimmah, and Eden son of Joah.
verses.29:13: And of the sons of Elizaphan, Shimri and Jehiel. Also of the sons of Asaph, Zechariah and Mattaniah,
verses.29:14: as well as of the sons of Heman, Jehiel and Shimei; and of the sons of Jeduthun also, Shemaiah and Uzziel.
verses.29:15: And they gathered their brothers and sanctified themselves, and entered according to the command of the king and the decree of the Lord, to purify the house of God.
verses.29:16: The priests also entered the temple of the Lord to sanctify it, and brought out into the vestibule of the house of the Lord all the uncleanness that they had found inside; and the Levites took it and carried it outside to the Kidron brook.
verses.29:17: Now they began to cleanse on the first day of the first month, and on the eighth day of the same month they entered the portico of the temple of the Lord, and they purified the temple for eight days, and on the sixteenth day of the same month they completed what they had begun.
verses.29:18: They also went in to King Hezekiah and said to him, "We have sanctified the entire house of the Lord, and the altar of burnt offering and its vessels, as well as the table of showbread with all its vessels,
verses.29:19: and all the furnishings of the temple, which King Ahaz had defiled during his reign, after he transgressed; and look, all of them are set out before the altar of the Lord."
verses.29:20: And rising at dawn, King Hezekiah assembled all the leaders of the city and went up to the house of the Lord;
verses.29:21: and they presented together seven bulls, and seven rams, seven lambs, and seven male goats for a sin offering, for the kingdom, for the sanctuary, for Judah; and he told the priests, the sons of Aaron, to offer them on the altar of the Lord.
verses.29:22: Therefore they slaughtered the bulls, and the priests received the blood and poured it upon the altar; they also slaughtered the rams and poured their blood upon the altar, and they sacrificed the lambs and poured the blood upon the altar.
verses.29:23: They brought forward the male goats for the sin offering before the king and the entire multitude, and laid their hands on them;
verses.29:24: and the priests sacrificed them and sprinkled their blood before the altar for the atonement of all Israel; for the king had commanded that the burnt offering and the sin offering be made for all Israel.
verses.29:25: He also stationed the Levites in the house of the Lord with cymbals, harps, and lyres, according to the arrangement of King David, and of Gad the seer, and of Nathan the prophet; for indeed it was the command of the Lord through the hand of His prophets.
verses.29:26: And the Levites stood holding the instruments of David, and the priests the trumpets.
verses.29:27: And Hezekiah ordered that they offer the burnt offerings on the altar; and while the burnt offerings were being offered, they began to sing praises to the Lord, and to sound the trumpets, and to play loudly on the various instruments that David king of Israel had prepared.
verses.29:28: Now while the whole crowd was worshiping, the singers and those who held the trumpets were at their duty until the burnt offering was completed.
verses.29:29: And when the offering was finished, the king and all who were with him bowed down and worshiped.
verses.29:30: And Hezekiah and the leaders commanded the Levites to praise the Lord with the words of David and of Asaph the seer; and they praised Him with great joy, and bowing the knee, they worshiped.
verses.29:31: And Hezekiah added these words as well: "You have filled your hands for the Lord; come near, and offer victims and praises in the house of the Lord." Therefore the entire multitude offered sacrifices, and praises, and burnt offerings, with a devoted mind.
verses.29:32: Furthermore, the number of the burnt offerings that the multitude offered was this: seventy bulls, one hundred rams, and two hundred lambs.
verses.29:33: And they sanctified to the Lord six hundred oxen and three thousand sheep.
verses.29:34: However, the priests were few, and were not sufficient to strip off the hides of the burnt offerings; so the Levites their brothers also helped them until the work was completed and the priests were sanctified, for the Levites are sanctified by an easier rite than the priests.
verses.29:35: Therefore there were very many burnt offerings, the fat portions of the peace offerings, and the drink offerings of the burnt offerings; and the worship of the house of the Lord was completed.
verses.29:36: And Hezekiah and all the people rejoiced, because the service of the Lord had been fulfilled; for indeed it had seemed good for this to happen suddenly.
verses.30:1: Hezekiah also sent to all Israel and Judah, and wrote letters to Ephraim and Manasseh, that they should come to the house of the Lord in Jerusalem and keep the Passover to the Lord God of Israel.
verses.30:2: Therefore, after the king and the princes and the whole assembly of Jerusalem had taken counsel, they decreed to keep the Passover in the second month.
verses.30:3: For they had not been able to keep it at its proper time, because priests who could suffice had not been sanctified, and the people had not yet been gathered in Jerusalem.
verses.30:4: And the matter pleased the king and the whole multitude.
verses.30:5: And they decreed to send messengers throughout all Israel, from Beersheba to Dan, that they should come and keep the Passover to the Lord God of Israel in Jerusalem; for many had not kept it as was prescribed by the law.
verses.30:6: And the couriers went out with letters by the command of the king and his princes throughout all Israel and Judah, according to what the king had ordered, proclaiming, "Sons of Israel, return to the Lord God of Abraham, Isaac, and Israel, and He will return to the remnant that has escaped the hand of the king of the Assyrians.
verses.30:7: Do not become like your fathers and brothers, who departed from the Lord God of their fathers, who gave them over to destruction, as you yourselves see.
verses.30:8: Do not harden your necks, as your fathers did; yield your hands to the Lord, and come to His sanctuary, which He has sanctified forever; serve the Lord God of your fathers, and the wrath of His fury will be turned away from you.
verses.30:9: For if you return to the Lord, your brothers and sons will receive mercy before their masters who led them captive, and they will return to this land; for the Lord your God is compassionate and merciful, and He will not turn His face away from you if you return to Him."
verses.30:10: So the couriers traveled swiftly from city to city through the land of Ephraim and Manasseh as far as Zebulun, while those people laughed at and mocked them.
verses.30:11: Nevertheless, certain men from Asher, Manasseh, and Zebulun, consenting to the counsel, came to Jerusalem.
verses.30:12: In Judah, however, the hand of the Lord was present to give them one heart, so that they might carry out the word of the Lord according to the command of the king and the princes.
verses.30:13: And many people were gathered in Jerusalem to keep the feast of unleavened bread in the second month.
verses.30:14: And rising up, they destroyed the altars that were in Jerusalem, and overturning all the things on which incense was burned to idols, they threw them into the brook Kidron.
verses.30:15: Then they sacrificed the Passover on the fourteenth day of the second month. The priests also and the Levites, at last sanctified, offered burnt offerings in the house of the Lord.
verses.30:16: And they stood in their order according to the ordinance and the law of Moses, the man of God; and the priests received from the hands of the Levites the blood to be poured out,
verses.30:17: because a large crowd had not been sanctified, and therefore the Levites sacrificed the Passover for those who had not come in time to be sanctified to the Lord.
verses.30:18: Also a great part of the people from Ephraim, Manasseh, Issachar, and Zebulun, who had not been sanctified, ate the Passover not according to what is written; and Hezekiah prayed for them, saying, "The good Lord will be merciful
verses.30:19: to all who with their whole heart seek the Lord God of their fathers, and will not count it against them that they were insufficiently sanctified."
verses.30:20: And the Lord heard him, and was appeased toward the people.
verses.30:21: And the sons of Israel who were found in Jerusalem kept the feast of unleavened bread for seven days with great gladness, praising the Lord day by day, the Levites also and the priests with instruments that suited their office.
verses.30:22: And Hezekiah spoke to the heart of all the Levites who had good understanding concerning the Lord. And they ate for the seven days of the feast, sacrificing victims of peace offerings and praising the Lord God of their fathers.
verses.30:23: And it pleased the whole multitude to celebrate another seven days as well, which they indeed did with immense joy.
verses.30:24: For Hezekiah, king of Judah, had provided for the multitude a thousand bulls and seven thousand sheep, and the princes had given to the people a thousand bulls and ten thousand sheep; therefore a very great multitude of priests was sanctified.
verses.30:25: And the entire crowd of Judah was filled with cheerfulness, both the priests and the Levites, and the whole gathering that had come from Israel, as well as the proselytes from the land of Israel and those dwelling in Judah.
verses.30:26: And there was a great celebration in Jerusalem, such as had not been in that city since the days of Solomon, the son of David, king of Israel.
verses.30:27: Then the priests and the Levites rose up, blessing the people; and their voice was heard, and the prayer reached the holy dwelling place of heaven.
verses.31:1: And when these things had been duly celebrated, all Israel who had been found in the cities of Judah went out, and they broke the images, and cut down the groves, demolished the high places, and destroyed the altars, not only from all Judah and Benjamin, but also from Ephraim and Manasseh, until they had completely overthrown them; and all the sons of Israel returned to their possessions and their cities.
verses.31:2: Now Hezekiah appointed the priestly and Levitical companies according to their divisions, each one in his own office, namely both of the priests and of the Levites, for burnt offerings and peace offerings, to minister and to give thanks and to sing in the gates of the camps of the Lord.
verses.31:3: And the king's portion was that from his own property the burnt offering should be offered, always in the morning and in the evening, on the Sabbaths also, and on the first days of the months, and on the other feasts, as it is written in the law of Moses.
verses.31:4: He also commanded the people dwelling in Jerusalem to give the portions to the priests and the Levites, so that they might devote themselves to the law of the Lord.
verses.31:5: And when this had spread abroad in the ears of the multitude, the sons of Israel offered abundant firstfruits of grain, wine, and oil; of honey also, and of all things that the ground produces, they offered tithes.
verses.31:6: Moreover, the sons of Israel and Judah who lived in the cities of Judah offered tithes of oxen and sheep, and tithes of the holy things that they had vowed to the Lord their God; and bringing them all, they made very many heaps.
verses.31:7: In the third month they began to lay the foundations of the heaps, and in the seventh month they completed them.
verses.31:8: And when Hezekiah and his princes had come in, they saw the heaps, and they blessed the Lord and the people of Israel.
verses.31:9: And Hezekiah asked the priests and the Levites why the heaps were lying like that.
verses.31:10: Azariah, the chief priest of the lineage of Zadok, answered him, saying, "Since the firstfruits began to be offered in the house of the Lord, we have eaten and been satisfied, and very much has remained, because the Lord has blessed His people; and this that you see is the abundance of what remains."
verses.31:11: Therefore Hezekiah commanded that they prepare storerooms in the house of the Lord. And when they had done this,
verses.31:12: they faithfully brought in both the firstfruits and the tithes, and whatever they had vowed. And Conaniah the Levite was overseer over them, and Shimei his brother was second,
verses.31:13: after whom Jehiel, Azariah, Nahath, Asahel, Jerimoth, Jozabad also, Eliel, Ismachiah, Mahath, and Benaiah were supervisors under the hands of Conaniah and Shimei his brother, by the command of King Hezekiah and of Azariah, the high priest of the house of God, to whom all things pertained.
verses.31:14: Now Kore, the son of Imnah, a Levite and gatekeeper of the eastern gate, was in charge of the things that were freely offered to the Lord, and of the firstfruits and the things consecrated for the Holy of Holies.
verses.31:15: And under his care Eden, Benjamin, Jeshua, Shemaiah, Amariah also, and Shecaniah were in the cities of the priests, to faithfully distribute portions to their brothers, both small and great:
verses.31:16: apart from the males from three years old and upward, all who entered the temple of the Lord, and whatever was needed day by day in the ministry and the observances according to their divisions,
verses.31:17: to the priests by their families, and to the Levites from the twentieth year and upward, by their orders and companies,
verses.31:18: and to the whole multitude, both their wives and their children of both sexes, food from the things that had been sanctified was faithfully provided.
verses.31:19: And also throughout the fields of the sons of Aaron and the outskirts of each city, men were stationed to distribute portions to every male among the priests and the Levites.
verses.31:20: Therefore Hezekiah did all the things that we have said throughout all Judah; and he performed what was good and right and true before the Lord his God,
verses.31:21: in all the worship of the ministry of the house of the Lord, according to the law and the ceremonies, desiring to seek his God with his whole heart; and he did so, and prospered.
verses.32:1: After these events and truthfulness of this sort, Sennacherib, king of the Assyrians, came, and having entered Judah, he besieged the fortified cities, wishing to capture them.
verses.32:2: When Hezekiah saw this, namely that Sennacherib had arrived and that the whole thrust of the war was being turned against Jerusalem,
verses.32:3: having taken counsel with the leaders and the bravest men in order to block up the heads of the springs that were outside the city, and as the judgment of everyone decided upon this,
verses.32:4: he assembled a very large crowd, and they blocked up all the springs and the stream that flowed through the middle of the land, saying, "Let the kings of the Assyrians not come and find an abundance of waters."
verses.32:5: Acting diligently, he also built up every wall that had been broken down, erected towers above it, and constructed another wall on the outside; he restored Millo in the city of David and fashioned weaponry of every kind and shields.
verses.32:6: He appointed commanders of the warriors in the army, summoned all of them into the open square of the city gate, and spoke to their heart, saying,
verses.32:7: "Act courageously and be strengthened; do not be afraid, nor be terrified of the king of the Assyrians and the entire throng that is with him, for far more are with us than with him.
verses.32:8: For with him is an arm of flesh, while with us is the Lord our God, who is our helper and fights on our behalf." And the people were strengthened by words of this sort from Hezekiah, king of Judah.
verses.32:9: After these things had taken place, Sennacherib, king of the Assyrians, sent his servants to Jerusalem (for he himself with his entire army was besieging Lachish) to Hezekiah, king of Judah, and to all the people who were in the city, saying,
verses.32:10: "Sennacherib, king of the Assyrians, declares these things: In what are you placing confidence as you sit besieged in Jerusalem?
verses.32:11: Is Hezekiah deceiving you to hand you over to death in hunger and thirst, asserting that the Lord your God will free you from the hand of the king of the Assyrians?
verses.32:12: Is this not that very Hezekiah who tore down His high places and altars, and instructed Judah and Jerusalem, saying, 'Before a single altar you will worship, and upon it you will burn incense'?
verses.32:13: Or are you unaware of what I and my fathers have done to all the peoples of the lands? Did the gods of the nations and of all the lands prevail to free their territory from my hand?
verses.32:14: Who is there among all the gods of the nations that my fathers laid waste who was able to rescue his people from my hand, so that your God also could rescue you from this hand?
verses.32:15: Therefore, do not let Hezekiah deceive you, nor mislead you with empty persuasion, and do not believe him. For if no god of all the nations and kingdoms was able to free his people from my hand and from the hand of my fathers, consequently neither will your God be able to rescue you from my hand."
verses.32:16: Moreover, his servants spoke many other things against the Lord God and against His servant Hezekiah.
verses.32:17: He also wrote letters filled with blasphemy against the Lord God of Israel, and spoke against Him: "Just as the gods of the remaining nations could not free their people from my hand, so too the God of Hezekiah will not be able to rescue His people from this hand."
verses.32:18: In addition, with a loud cry in the Judean language, he called out against the people who were sitting upon the walls of Jerusalem, so as to terrify them and capture the city.
verses.32:19: And he spoke against the God of Jerusalem just as against the gods of the peoples of the earth, the works of human hands.
verses.32:20: King Hezekiah and Isaiah son of Amoz, the prophet, therefore prayed against this blasphemy, and cried aloud all the way to heaven.
verses.32:21: And the Lord dispatched an angel, who struck down every stalwart man, warrior, and commander of the army of the king of the Assyrians; and he returned in disgrace to his own land. And when he had entered the house of his god, sons who had issued from his own body killed him with the sword.
verses.32:22: Thus the Lord saved Hezekiah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem from the hand of Sennacherib, king of the Assyrians, and from the hand of everyone, and granted them rest on every side.
verses.32:23: Many also brought victims and sacrifices to the Lord in Jerusalem, along with gifts to Hezekiah, king of Judah; and after these events he was exalted before all the nations.
verses.32:24: In those days Hezekiah fell ill to the point of death, and he prayed to the Lord; and He heard him and gave him a sign.
verses.32:25: Yet he did not repay according to the benefits he had received, because his heart was lifted up; and wrath arose against him, and against Judah and Jerusalem.
verses.32:26: Afterward, however, he humbled himself because his heart had been exalted, both he and the inhabitants of Jerusalem; and for that reason the wrath of the Lord did not come upon them during the days of Hezekiah.
verses.32:27: Now Hezekiah was wealthy and exceedingly renowned, and he gathered for himself abundant treasuries of silver and gold, of precious stone, of spices, of weapons of every sort, and of vessels of great worth.
verses.32:28: Storehouses as well for grain, wine, and oil, and stalls for all beasts of burden, and folds for flocks,
verses.32:29: and cities he built for himself; for indeed he owned countless flocks of sheep and herds of cattle, because the Lord had bestowed upon him exceedingly abundant wealth.
verses.32:30: This same Hezekiah is the one who blocked up the upper spring of the waters of Gihon and directed them underground toward the west side of the city of David; in all his works he carried out prosperously what he desired.
verses.32:31: Nevertheless, regarding the embassy of the princes of Babylon who had been sent to him to inquire about the portent that had occurred upon the land, God left him alone so that he might be tested, and that everything in his heart might become known.
verses.32:32: Now the remainder of the accounts of Hezekiah and of his acts of mercy are recorded in the vision of Isaiah son of Amoz, the prophet, and in the book of the kings of Judah and Israel.
verses.32:33: And Hezekiah slept with his fathers, and they buried him above the tombs of the sons of David; and all Judah and all the inhabitants of Jerusalem celebrated his funeral rites, and his son Manasseh reigned in his place.
verses.33:1: Manasseh was twelve years of age when he began to reign, and for fifty-five years he reigned in Jerusalem.
verses.33:2: Yet he did evil before the Lord, according to the abominations of the nations that the Lord overthrew before the sons of Israel.
verses.33:3: Turning back, he restored the high places that his father Hezekiah had demolished; he erected altars to the Baals, made sacred groves, and worshiped the entire host of heaven and served it.
verses.33:4: He also constructed altars in the house of the Lord, concerning which the Lord had said, "In Jerusalem My name will be forever."
verses.33:5: Indeed, he built them for the entire army of heaven in the two courtyards of the house of the Lord.
verses.33:6: He also caused his sons to pass through fire in the valley of Ben-hinnom; he observed dreams, pursued omens, devoted himself to wicked arts, kept magicians and enchanters with him, and carried out many evil deeds before the Lord to provoke Him.
verses.33:7: He also set a carved and cast image in the house of God, concerning which God spoke to David and to his son Solomon, saying, "In this house, and in Jerusalem, which I have chosen out of all the tribes of Israel, I will place My name perpetually.
verses.33:8: And I will not cause the foot of Israel to be moved from the land that I delivered to their fathers, provided only that they take care to carry out what I have commanded them, and the entire law, and the ceremonies and judgments, through the hand of Moses."
verses.33:9: Thus Manasseh led Judah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem astray, so that they practiced evil beyond all the nations that the Lord had overthrown from before the face of the sons of Israel.
verses.33:10: And the Lord spoke to him and to his people, yet they refused to pay heed.
verses.33:11: For that reason He brought upon them the commanders of the army of the king of the Assyrians; and they seized Manasseh, and bound in chains and shackles, they led him away into Babylon.
verses.33:12: After he was brought into dire distress, he prayed to the Lord his God and did deep penance before the God of his fathers.
verses.33:13: He pleaded with Him and implored earnestly; and He heard his prayer and brought him back to Jerusalem into his kingdom, and Manasseh recognized that the Lord Himself was God.
verses.33:14: After these events he constructed a wall outside the city of David, to the west of Gihon in the valley, from the entrance of the Fish Gate all around as far as Ophel, and raised it very high; and he stationed commanders of the army in all the fortified cities of Judah.
verses.33:15: He also removed the foreign gods and the idol from the house of the Lord, together with the altars that he had built on the mountain of the house of the Lord and in Jerusalem, and cast them all outside the city.
verses.33:16: Furthermore, he restored the altar of the Lord and sacrificed upon it victims, peace offerings, and praise; and he commanded Judah to serve the Lord, the God of Israel.
verses.33:17: Even so, the people still offered sacrifices at the high places to the Lord their God.
verses.33:18: Now the rest of the deeds of Manasseh, and his supplication to his God, and also the words of the seers who spoke to him in the name of the Lord, the God of Israel, are contained in the records of the kings of Israel.
verses.33:19: His prayer as well and its favorable hearing, and all his sins and acts of contempt, and also the sites where he built high places and made sacred groves and statues before he did penance, are written in the records of Hozai.
verses.33:20: So Manasseh slept with his fathers, and they buried him in his own house; and his son Amon reigned in his place.
verses.33:21: Amon was twenty-two years of age when he began to reign, and for two years he reigned in Jerusalem.
verses.33:22: And he did evil in the sight of the Lord, just as his father Manasseh had done; and to all the idols that Manasseh had crafted, he sacrificed and rendered service.
verses.33:23: Yet he did not show reverence before the face of the Lord, as his father Manasseh had shown reverence, and he committed far greater offenses.
verses.33:24: And after his servants conspired against him, they killed him in his own house.
verses.33:25: Then the remaining multitude of the people, having put to death those who had struck down Amon, established his son Josiah as king in his place.
verses.34:1: Josiah was eight years old when he began to reign, and he reigned in Jerusalem for thirty-one years.
verses.34:2: And he did what was right in the sight of the Lord and walked in the ways of David his father; he turned aside neither to the right nor to the left.
verses.34:3: Now in the eighth year of his reign, while he was still a boy, he began to seek the God of his father David; and in the twelfth year after he had begun to reign, he cleansed Judah and Jerusalem from the high places and the sacred groves, and the statues and the carved images.
verses.34:4: And they destroyed the altars of the Baals in his presence, and they demolished the statues that had been set upon them; he also cut down and crushed to pieces the sacred groves and the carved images, and scattered the fragments over the graves of those who had been accustomed to sacrifice to them.
verses.34:5: Moreover, he burned the bones of the priests on the altars of the idols, and cleansed Judah and Jerusalem.
verses.34:6: And also in the cities of Manasseh, Ephraim, and Simeon, as far as Naphtali, he overturned everything.
verses.34:7: And when he had torn down the altars, and crushed the sacred groves and the carved images into pieces, and demolished all the shrines from the entire land of Israel, he returned to Jerusalem.
verses.34:8: Therefore, in the eighteenth year of his reign, now that the land and the temple of the Lord had been cleansed, he sent Shaphan the son of Azaliah, and Maaseiah the governor of the city, and Joah the son of Joahaz, the keeper of records, to restore the house of the Lord his God.
verses.34:9: They came to Hilkiah the high priest; and having received from him the money that had been brought into the house of the Lord, and that the Levites and the gatekeepers had gathered from Manasseh and Ephraim and all the remnant of Israel, and also from all Judah and Benjamin and the inhabitants of Jerusalem,
verses.34:10: they delivered it into the hands of those who were over the workers in the house of the Lord, so that they might restore the temple and mend whatever was weak.
verses.34:11: And they gave it to the craftsmen and the masons to buy stones from the quarries, and timber for the joints of the building and for the beamwork of the houses that the kings of Judah had destroyed.
verses.34:12: They did everything faithfully. Now the overseers of the workers were Jahath and Obadiah of the sons of Merari, Zechariah and Meshullam of the sons of Kohath, who pressed the work forward: all Levites who knew how to play musical instruments.
verses.34:13: And over those who carried burdens for various uses, there were scribes and officers from the Levites, and gatekeepers.
verses.34:14: And while they were bringing out the money that had been brought into the temple of the Lord, Hilkiah the priest found the book of the law of the Lord by the hand of Moses.
verses.34:15: And he said to Shaphan the scribe, "I have found the book of the law in the house of the Lord." And he delivered it to him.
verses.34:16: And he brought the scroll to the king and reported to him, saying, "Look, everything that you placed in the hand of your servants is being carried out.
verses.34:17: They have melted down the silver that was found in the house of the Lord, and it has been given to the overseers of the craftsmen and of those who fashion the various works.
verses.34:18: Moreover, Hilkiah the priest delivered this book to me." And when he had read it aloud in the presence of the king,
verses.34:19: and the king had heard the words of the law, he tore his garments,
verses.34:20: and commanded Hilkiah, and Ahikam the son of Shaphan, and Abdon the son of Micah, and also Shaphan the scribe, and Asaiah the king's servant, saying,
verses.34:21: "Go and pray to the Lord for me, and for the remnant of Israel and Judah, concerning all the words of this book that has been found; for the great fury of the Lord has poured down upon us, because our fathers did not keep the words of the Lord, to do all that is written in this scroll."
verses.34:22: So Hilkiah and those who had been sent together by the king went to Huldah the prophetess, the wife of Shallum the son of Tokhath, the son of Hasrah, keeper of the garments, who lived in Jerusalem in the Second District; and they spoke to her the words that we have recounted above.
verses.34:23: And she answered them, "This is what the Lord God of Israel says: Tell the man who sent you to me,
verses.34:24: 'This is what the Lord says: Look, I will bring evils upon this place and upon its inhabitants, and all the curses that are written in this book which they read before the king of Judah.
verses.34:25: Because they have abandoned Me and have sacrificed to foreign gods, to provoke Me to anger in all the works of their hands, therefore My fury will pour down upon this place and will not be extinguished.'
verses.34:26: But to the king of Judah, who sent you to implore the Lord, speak in this way: 'This is what the Lord God of Israel says: Because you have heard the words of the scroll,
verses.34:27: and your heart was softened, and you humbled yourself in the sight of God concerning the things that were spoken against this place and the inhabitants of Jerusalem, and revering My face you tore your garments and wept before Me, I also have heard you, says the Lord.
verses.34:28: For now I will gather you to your fathers, and you will be carried into your tomb in peace, and your eyes will not see all the evil that I am about to bring upon this place and upon its inhabitants.'" So they reported back to the king everything that she had said.
verses.34:29: Then he, having summoned all the elders of Judah and Jerusalem,
verses.34:30: went up into the house of the Lord, and together with him all the men of Judah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem, the priests and the Levites, and all the people from the least to the greatest. While they listened in the house of the Lord, the king read all the words of the scroll.
verses.34:31: And standing on his platform, he made a covenant before the Lord to walk after Him and to keep His commandments, testimonies, and statutes with all his heart and with all his soul, and to do the things that are written in that scroll which he had read.
verses.34:32: He also placed under oath concerning this all who were found in Jerusalem and Benjamin; and the inhabitants of Jerusalem acted according to the covenant of the Lord God of their fathers.
verses.34:33: Therefore Josiah removed all the abominations from all the regions of the sons of Israel, and made all who remained in Israel serve the Lord their God. All his days they did not depart from the Lord God of their fathers.
verses.35:1: Now Josiah kept a Passover to the Lord in Jerusalem, which was sacrificed on the fourteenth day of the first month.
verses.35:2: And he appointed the priests in their offices and encouraged them to minister in the house of the Lord.
verses.35:3: To the Levites also, by whose instruction all Israel was sanctified to the Lord, he said, "Put the ark in the sanctuary of the temple that Solomon the son of David, king of Israel, built, for you will no longer carry it at all; now, however, minister to the Lord your God and to His people Israel.
verses.35:4: And prepare yourselves according to your houses and clans, in the divisions of each one, just as David king of Israel commanded and Solomon his son wrote down.
verses.35:5: And minister in the sanctuary by families and Levitical companies,
verses.35:6: and being sanctified, sacrifice the Passover; and also prepare your brothers, so that they may be able to act according to the words that the Lord spoke by the hand of Moses."
verses.35:7: Moreover, Josiah gave to all the people who had been found there at the festival of the Passover lambs and young goats from the flocks and of the rest of the small livestock, thirty thousand, and also three thousand oxen; these were from all the king's possessions.
verses.35:8: His leaders also willingly offered what they had vowed, both to the people and to the priests and the Levites. Furthermore, Hilkiah, Zechariah, and Jehiel, the rulers of the house of the Lord, gave to the priests for keeping the Passover small livestock mixed together, two thousand six hundred, and three hundred oxen.
verses.35:9: And Conaniah, and Shemaiah and also Nethanel his brothers, as well as Hashabiah, Jehiel, and Jozabad, the rulers of the Levites, gave to the rest of the Levites for celebrating the Passover five thousand small livestock and five hundred oxen.
verses.35:10: And the ministry was prepared, and the priests stood in their office, and the Levites also in companies, according to the king's command.
verses.35:11: And the Passover was sacrificed; and the priests sprinkled the blood with their hand, and the Levites stripped off the skins of the burnt offerings.
verses.35:12: And they set them apart to give them by the houses and families of each one, so that they might be offered to the Lord, just as is written in the book of Moses; and they did likewise with the oxen also.
verses.35:13: And they roasted the Passover over the fire, according to what is written in the law; while the peace offerings they boiled in cauldrons, kettles, and pots, and hastily distributed them to the whole populace.
verses.35:14: For themselves and for the priests, however, they prepared afterward, for the priests were occupied until night in the offering of the burnt offerings and the fat; therefore the Levites prepared last of all for themselves and for the priests, the sons of Aaron.
verses.35:15: Furthermore, the singers, the sons of Asaph, stood in their order according to the command of David, and of Asaph, Heman, and Jeduthun, the prophets of the king; and the gatekeepers kept watch at each gate, so that they did not depart from their ministry even for a moment; for this reason their brothers the Levites also prepared food for them.
verses.35:16: Therefore all the worship of the Lord was duly completed on that day, to keep the Passover and to offer burnt offerings on the altar of the Lord, according to the command of King Josiah.
verses.35:17: And the sons of Israel who had been found there kept the Passover at that time, and the festival of unleavened bread for seven days.
verses.35:18: There was no Passover like this in Israel from the days of Samuel the prophet; nor did any of all the kings of Israel keep a Passover like Josiah did for the priests, and the Levites, and all Judah and Israel who had been found, and those living in Jerusalem.
verses.35:19: In the eighteenth year of the reign of Josiah this Passover was celebrated.
verses.35:20: After Josiah had restored the temple, Necho king of Egypt went up to fight at Carchemish by the Euphrates, and Josiah went out to meet him.
verses.35:21: But he, having sent messengers to him, said, "What have I to do with you, king of Judah? I am not coming against you today, but I am fighting against another house, to which God has commanded me to go in haste; cease acting against God, who is with me, so that He may not kill you."
verses.35:22: Josiah refused to turn back, but prepared war against him, and did not yield to the words of Necho from the mouth of God; instead, he proceeded to fight in the plain of Megiddo.
verses.35:23: And there, wounded by the archers, he said to his servants, "Take me out of the battle, for I am severely wounded."
verses.35:24: They transferred him from the chariot into another chariot, which followed him according to royal custom, and carried him away to Jerusalem; and he died and was buried in the mausoleum of his fathers, and all Judah and Jerusalem mourned for him.
verses.35:25: Jeremiah most of all: all the male and female singers repeat his lamentations over Josiah up to the present day, and it has prevailed like a law in Israel. Look, it is said to be written in the Lamentations.
verses.35:26: Now the rest of the words of Josiah, and of his mercies, which are commanded by the law of the Lord,
verses.35:27: and also his works, first and last, are written in the book of the kings of Judah and Israel.
verses.36:1: Therefore the people of the land took Jehoahaz, the son of Josiah, and appointed him king in place of his father in Jerusalem.
verses.36:2: Jehoahaz was twenty-three years old when he began to reign, and he reigned in Jerusalem for three months.
verses.36:3: Now the king of Egypt removed him when he had come to Jerusalem, and fined the land one hundred talents of silver and a talent of gold.
verses.36:4: And he appointed Eliakim his brother king in his place over Judah and Jerusalem, and changed his name to Jehoiakim; but Jehoahaz himself he took with him and led away into Egypt.
verses.36:5: Jehoiakim was twenty-five years old when he began to reign, and he reigned in Jerusalem for eleven years; and he did evil before the Lord his God.
verses.36:6: Nebuchadnezzar, king of the Chaldeans, came up against him and led him, bound in chains, into Babylon.
verses.36:7: To it he also carried the vessels of the Lord and placed them in his temple.
verses.36:8: Now the rest of the deeds of Jehoiakim, and his abominations which he practiced, and what was found in him, are contained in the book of the kings of Judah and Israel. And Jehoiachin his son reigned in his place.
verses.36:9: Jehoiachin was eight years old when he began to reign, and he reigned in Jerusalem for three months and ten days; and he did evil in the sight of the Lord.
verses.36:10: And when the circuit of the year came around, King Nebuchadnezzar sent men who brought him into Babylon, with the most precious vessels of the house of the Lord carried off at the same time. And he appointed Zedekiah his uncle king over Judah and Jerusalem.
verses.36:11: Zedekiah was twenty-one years old when he began to reign, and he reigned in Jerusalem for eleven years.
verses.36:12: And he did evil in the eyes of the Lord his God, and he was not ashamed before the face of Jeremiah the prophet, speaking to him from the mouth of the Lord.
verses.36:13: He also broke away from King Nebuchadnezzar, who had put him under oath by God; and he hardened his neck and heart so that he would not return to the Lord God of Israel.
verses.36:14: Moreover, all the leaders of the priests and the people transgressed wickedly according to all the abominations of the nations, and polluted the house of the Lord, which He had sanctified for Himself in Jerusalem.
verses.36:15: Now the Lord God of their fathers kept sending to them by the hand of His messengers, rising up in the night and warning them daily, because He was sparing His people and His dwelling place.
verses.36:16: But they mocked the messengers of God, and made light of His words, and scoffed at the prophets, until the fury of the Lord rose up against His people, and there was no healing.
verses.36:17: For He brought upon them the king of the Chaldeans, and killed their young men with the sword in the house of His sanctuary; He had no compassion on youth, or virgin, or old man, nor even on one who was decrepit, but He handed them all over into his hands.
verses.36:18: And all the vessels of the house of the Lord, both large and small, and the treasures of the temple, and of the king, and of the leaders, he carried into Babylon.
verses.36:19: The enemies set fire to the house of God and tore down the wall of Jerusalem; they burned down all the towers, and they demolished whatever had been precious.
verses.36:20: If anyone had escaped the sword, he was led into Babylon and served the king and his sons, until the king of the Persians ruled,
verses.36:21: and the word of the Lord from the mouth of Jeremiah was fulfilled, and the land celebrated its Sabbaths; for it kept Sabbath all the days of desolation, until seventy years were fulfilled.
verses.36:22: Now in the first year of Cyrus, king of the Persians, to fulfill the word of the Lord which He had spoken through the mouth of Jeremiah, the Lord stirred up the spirit of Cyrus, king of the Persians, who ordered it to be proclaimed throughout his entire kingdom, even in writing, saying:
verses.36:23: "This is what Cyrus, king of the Persians, says: The Lord God of heaven has given me all the kingdoms of the earth, and He Himself has commanded me to build a house for Him in Jerusalem, which is in Judea. Who of you is among all His people? May the Lord his God be with him, and let him go up."

notes.1:2: Latin uses Roman military titles (tribunis, et centurionibus, 'tribunes and centurions') for the Hebrew commanders of thousands and hundreds, and reads praecepit ('gave orders') where the Hebrew has 'spoke.'
notes.1:3: Latin tabernaculum foederis ('tent of the covenant,' also in 1:6, 1:13) is a distinctly Vulgate rendering of Hebrew 'tent of meeting.'
notes.1:13: Latin reads in Jerusalem coram tabernaculo foederis ('to Jerusalem, before the tent of the covenant'), placing coram ('before') after in Jerusalem rather than 'from before the tent of meeting' as in the Hebrew.
notes.1:17: Distinctly Vulgate reading: Latin de universis regnis Hethaeorum, et a regibus Syriae emptio celebrabatur describes purchasing horses and four-horse chariots from all the kingdoms of the Hittites and from the kings of Syria, whereas the Hebrew describes exporting them to the kings of the Hittites and Aram.
notes.1:18: In the Vulgate chapter division, 1:18 corresponds to 2:1 in the Hebrew Masoretic Text (shifting the verse numbers of chapter 2 by one); Latin also renders Hebrew 'house for his kingdom' as palatium ('palace').
notes.2:7: Latin renders the three kinds of Lebanon timber as cedrina (cedar), arceuthina (juniper), and pinea (pine), whereas the Hebrew lists cedar, cypress, and algum trees.
notes.2:9: Latin uses three distinct units of measure—coros (kors) for wheat and barley, metretas (metretes, an ancient liquid measure) for wine, and sata (seahs) for oil—where the Hebrew uses baths for both wine and oil.
notes.2:12: Latin renders Hebrew Huram-abi literally as Hiram patrem meum ('Hiram my father'), reflecting an honorific title for a master craftsman while adopting the spelling Hiram.
notes.2:13: Latin specifies marmore ('marble,' as also in 3:6) where the Hebrew reads 'stones.'
notes.2:16: Latin renders Hebrew 'resident aliens' with the Septuagint-influenced term proselytos ('proselytes'), and divides the total as 'one hundred fifty thousand, and three thousand six hundred' in anticipation of 2:17.
notes.3:1: Distinctly Vulgate reading: Latin qui demonstratus fuerat David patri ejus ('which had been shown to David his father') makes Mount Moriah the subject shown to David, whereas the Hebrew reads 'where the Lord had appeared to David his father.'
notes.3:2: Latin omits 'on the second day' found in the Hebrew Masoretic Text, reading simply mense secundo, anno quarto regni sui ('in the second month, in the fourth year of his reign').
notes.3:7: Latin renders Hebrew 'gold of Parvaim' (at the end of 3:6 in the Hebrew) as aurum erat probatissimum ('the gold was most thoroughly tested') at the opening of 3:7.
notes.3:9: Latin uses distributive numerals (singuli clavi siclos quinquagenos), specifying that each individual nail weighed fifty shekels, whereas the Hebrew is commonly taken as fifty shekels for the weight of the nails.
notes.3:16: Latin in oraculo ('in the oracle') renders Hebrew debir, the inner sanctuary or Most Holy Place, understood by Jerome as the place of divine utterance.
notes.4:3: The Vulgate reads "for ten cubits" (decem cubitis) and "certain carvings on the outside" encircling the "belly" (alvum) of the sea, whereas the Hebrew describes ten figures per cubit encircling the sea and notes that the oxen were cast in a single casting with it.
notes.4:5: Latin metretas refers to the Greco-Roman liquid measure (roughly nine to ten gallons), which the Vulgate uses here for the Hebrew bath.
notes.4:12: Latin epistylia ("capitals/architraves") and capita ("heads/tops") render the Hebrew bowls and capitals atop the two pillars, with the Vulgate placing the heads above the capitals.
notes.4:16: Latin Hiram pater ejus ("Hiram his father") renders Hebrew Huram-abi, an honorific title ("master craftsman" or "counselor") rather than biological paternity; in 4:11 and 4:16 the Vulgate also reads creagras ("meat forks") where the Hebrew in 4:11 has "shovels."
notes.4:22: The Vulgate explicitly adds "he carved" (cælavit) and lists "small mortars" (mortariola), and includes the closing sentence ("And thus all the work...") in 4:22 rather than as the opening of 5:1 as in the Hebrew text.
notes.5:5: Latin omnem paraturam tabernaculi ("all the furnishings of the tabernacle") renders Hebrew "the tent of meeting," and "the priests with the Levites" separates two groups where the Hebrew reads "the Levitical priests."
notes.5:7: Latin oraculum (literally "oracle," the place of divine utterance, also in 4:20 and 5:9) is the Vulgate's regular rendering of Hebrew debir, the inner sanctuary of the temple.
notes.5:10: The Vulgate reads "when the Lord gave the law" (legem dedit) where the Hebrew reads "when the LORD made a covenant."
notes.5:11: The Vulgate states that the priestly courses and order of ministries had not yet been divided among them at that time, whereas the Hebrew indicates that the priests consecrated themselves without keeping to their divisions.
notes.5:13: The Vulgate expands the musical account with "voice," "instruments, and various kinds of music," and "the sound was heard far away," and in 5:14 shifts from "cloud" (nube) to "thick darkness" (caliginem).
notes.6:2: The Vulgate speaks of God in the third person ("for His name, so that He might dwell there"), whereas the Hebrew text addresses God directly in the second person.
notes.6:13: Latin basilicæ denotes a royal colonnaded hall or enclosed court, rendering the Hebrew term for the temple court.
notes.6:18: The Vulgate renders the a fortiori exclamation literally with quanto magis ("how much more [does this house fail to contain You]"), corresponding to the sense "how much less."
notes.6:19: The Vulgate adds the explanatory clause "Yet it has been made for this alone," which is not in the Hebrew text; similarly in 6:21, 6:30, and 6:39 it adds brief glosses ("that is," "namely") clarifying God's heavenly dwelling.
notes.6:40: The Vulgate reads "for You are my God" (tu es enim Deus meus), reflecting the Hebrew word for "you" rather than the homophonous word for "now."
notes.7:5: The Vulgate specifies arietum ("rams") where the Hebrew text uses the broader term for sheep or flocks.
notes.7:6: The phrase "by their hands" (per manus suas) literally reproduces a Hebrew idiom meaning "through their ministry" or "under their direction."
notes.7:14: The Vulgate reads conversus ("turning back") where the Hebrew text reads "humble themselves," and intensifies "wicked ways" with the superlative pessimis ("most wicked").
notes.7:21: The Vulgate reads erit in proverbium ("will become a proverb"), differing from the Hebrew text ("which was exalted").
notes.8:4: The Vulgate renders Hebrew Tadmor by its classical Greco-Roman name, Palmyram ("Palmyra"), and translates the Hebrew store cities as civitates munitissimas ("very strongly fortified cities"; similarly urbes firmissimas in 8:6).
notes.8:10: Latin principes exercitus ("commanders of the army") and qui erudiebant populum ("who instructed the people") are distinctly Vulgate readings where the Hebrew refers to chief officers exercising oversight over the people.
notes.8:13: Latin in calendis literally refers to the Kalends, the first days of each month, corresponding here to the monthly new-moon festivals in the Hebrew text.
notes.8:16: Latin Omnes impensas praeparatas habuit Salomon ("Solomon had all the expenses prepared") differs from the Hebrew, which speaks of all Solomon's work being carried out from the founding to the completion of the house.
notes.9:10: Latin ligna thyina ("thyine wood," an aromatic North African wood prized in antiquity) is the Vulgate rendering for Hebrew algum wood here and in 9:11.
notes.9:15: The Vulgate reads hastas aureas ("golden spears") and sexcentorum aureorum ("six hundred gold pieces") where the Hebrew describes large shields made with six hundred shekels of gold.
notes.9:16: Latin in armentario, quod erat consitum nemore ("in the armory, which was planted with a grove," with armentario as the Clementine form of armamentario) is Jerome's rendering of the House of the Forest of Lebanon, translated literally in 9:20 as domus saltus Libani.
notes.9:22: Latin gloria ("glory") is a Vulgate-distinct reading where the Hebrew text reads "wisdom."
notes.9:25: The Vulgate reads quadraginta millia ("forty thousand") horses in stables and twelve thousand chariots and horsemen, matching the higher figure of 1 Kings 4:26 rather than the four thousand stalls of the Hebrew text of 2 Chronicles.
notes.10:2: Latin statim reversus est ("he immediately returned") agrees in sense with 1 Kings 12:2 rather than the Hebrew text of 2 Chronicles 10:2, which states that Jeroboam dwelt in Egypt.
